title: Every non-Java language is parsed with a foreign grammar, silently
evidence: Cargo.toml:8-10 ships only tree-sitter-java and tree-sitter-javascript. src/ingestion/adapter/kotlin.rs:29-31 returns `tree_sitter_java::language()`, yet its map targets tree-sitter-kotlin kinds that the Java grammar never emits ('simple_identifier', '?:', '!!' at :35,57). Both registries fall back to a JavaScript-grammar adapter for any unregistered LangId (src/ingestion/adapter/registry.rs:34-39,56; src/ast/adapter/registry.rs:20-28,41). The AST registry has no Kotlin entry, so a .kt file is lexed as Java in Phase 1 and re-parsed as JavaScript in Phase 2 (src/ast/mod.rs:141-143). Python, TS, Rust, C++, Go, Swift, C# and the server's extra extensions (.sh, .sql, .asm; src/adapters/server.rs:805-866) all become JavaScript. Nothing in src/ calls has_error or is_missing.
impact: For every advertised non-Java language the parse tree is mostly ERROR nodes. Symbols, CFGs, SSA, the call graph and all diagrams are therefore artifacts of mis-parsing; for Kotlin, tokens and AST even come from two different grammars. Users get no warning.
recommendation: Ship real grammars (tree-sitter-kotlin-ng, -python, -typescript/tsx, -rust, -cpp, -go) after moving to tree-sitter 0.24+. Put them behind one registry with no JavaScript fallback; unsupported files are skipped with a diagnostic. Record per-file ERROR/MISSING node ratios (Node::has_error, Node::is_missing) in the .tca file record and the API response, and flag or exclude files above a threshold. Done = a per-language conformance corpus that parses with zero ERROR nodes, asserted in CI.

title: Kotlin and every non-Java language are parsed by different grammars in different phases; Phase 3 covers this with a raw-token keyword sweep
evidence: Phase 1 parses .kt files with tree_sitter_java (ingestion/adapter/kotlin.rs:29-31). Phase 2 has no Kotlin adapter and falls back to the JavaScript grammar (ast/adapter/registry.rs:19-28,41). Python, Rust, TS, C++ and Go use the JavaScript grammar in both phases (ingestion/adapter/registry.rs:29-39,56). Phase 2 then maps JS-grammar nodes onto Java-grammar tokens by (line, col). Phase 3 always uses JavaSemanticAdapter (symbol/mod.rs:38), plus a keyword sweep over raw tokens (pass1_discovery.rs:200-460). Symbols from the sweep have no decl_node, so Phase 4 skips them (cfg/mod.rs:55-58). The sweep turns `var`/`val` locals into SK_FIELDs (pass1_discovery.rs:414-450) and never resets current_class_sym per file (pass1_discovery.rs:257).
impact: Kotlin functions found by the sweep get no CFG, SSA, call edges or activity diagram. Kotlin and Java 10+ local variables appear as class fields. Top-level Kotlin functions attach to a class in another file. The multi-language claims rest on keyword heuristics.
recommendation: Create one LanguageRegistry (grammar, CST reducer, semantic adapter) keyed by LangId and used by Phases 1-3. Add pinned tree-sitter-kotlin and the other grammars, or reject unsupported extensions with a diagnostic. Remove the token sweep once Kotlin reduction exists. Per-language golden fixtures must assert classes, members and per-function CFG counts, plus a test that no SK_FIELD symbol lies inside a method body.

title: Server turns every panic, abort or hang into a remote outage (single-threaded inline pipeline)
evidence: start() runs handle_connection inline on the main thread (server.rs:40-42). There are no workers and no catch_unwind anywhere in src/. Sockets get a 500 ms read timeout but no write timeout (47). /api/analyze clones the repository and runs all ten phases synchronously, with no time or memory limit (241-253, 366-762). Consequences: a panic (ROB-05), a stack-overflow abort (ROB-08) or a hang (ROB-03) kills or wedges the service; each idle socket stalls it for 500 ms; a client that never reads blocks write_all forever. run.sh:34 serves the dev profile, where the debug_assert at token.rs:122 panics on a 16 MB file of newlines. Dockerfile:49 runs `serve`, which main.rs:544 rejects, so the container exits immediately.
impact: Every robustness defect in the analysis code becomes an unauthenticated one-request kill or hang of the default deployment, and any legitimate large analysis blocks all other users.
recommendation: Run each analysis as a job in a child process, or at minimum on a worker thread with catch_unwind and a 256 MB stack, under wall-clock and RSS limits (setrlimit, or Job Objects on Windows), with a bounded queue that returns 503 when full. Replace the hand-rolled loop with hyper/axum plus tower (TimeoutLayer, RequestBodyLimitLayer, ConcurrencyLimitLayer) and set socket write timeouts. Change the Docker CMD to `server 8080` and smoke-test the image in CI. Done when the ROB-03 and ROB-05 repros return an error and the server keeps serving.

title: Kotlin and 'six-language' support is illusory: Kotlin goes through the Java and JavaScript grammars, everything else through JavaScript
evidence: KotlinLanguageAdapter::ts_language() returns tree_sitter_java::language() (ingestion/adapter/kotlin.rs:29-31). Phase 2's registry has no Kotlin entry, so .kt falls back to the JavaScript grammar (ast/adapter/registry.rs:19-28). Kotlin is therefore tokenized as Java and reduced as JavaScript. Python, TypeScript, Rust and C++ have no adapters and also fall back to JavaScript (ingestion/adapter/registry.rs:34-39). The only grammar dependencies are java and javascript (Cargo.toml:9-11). The CLI ingests only .java/.kt/.kts (main.rs:76-99). Tests and examples contain zero non-Java fixtures, and ROADMAP.md:127 still lists C++/Rust/Go adapters as future work.
impact: Every Kotlin file yields wrong tokens and an AST that disagrees with Phase 1. Python, TypeScript, Rust and C++ input silently produces garbage. The README's F1 = 1.0000 claim is false for five of the six languages it names.
recommendation: Scope the README to Java now and label every other language experimental. Upgrade to tree-sitter 0.25+/0.26 with a current tree-sitter-java and a real Kotlin grammar (tree-sitter-kotlin-ng). Register one adapter per language for both Phase 1 and Phase 2 from a single table, and return an error instead of falling back to JavaScript for unknown extensions. Add per-language fixture suites in tree-sitter corpus style, and have CI track the rate of ERROR/MISSING nodes per file.

title: Language-neutral, compiler-grade rewiring of your paths (no hard-coding, no templates)
evidence: OpenHeart must support every language with language-agnostic algorithms, and must never hard-code, template or guess: it works the way compilers do, statically. New code is being written now (read what exists): src/lang (neutral.rs universal vocabulary, frontend.rs LanguageFrontend trait, registry.rs single list of languages, profile.rs, build/ for compile_commands, CMake and MSBuild, preprocess.rs, project_model.rs, uml_semantics.rs, idioms.rs, frontends java, kotlin, c, cpp, csharp); src/ir (typed three-address SSA IR with explicit memory operations, lowering from the AST, dominators); src/memory (abstract heap, field-sensitive points-to with on-the-fly call graph, escape, ownership, mod/ref); src/analysis (lattices, worklist solvers, SCCP, intervals, nullness, typestate, control dependence, IFDS/IDE, contexts, canonical branch conditions); src/derive (every diagram derived from those facts with provenance and a Derivation tag, NotDerivable instead of invention); src/symex (bounded static symbolic execution with a stack, heap and path-condition model producing execution traces); src/abi (C/C++ Itanium and MSVC, JVM and CLR memory layouts, lifetimes, calling conventions); src/arch (architecture recovery: dependency graph, DSM, layers, clustering, metrics, boundaries); src/memview (lifetime, ownership, heap-shape and stack-frame views plus memory-safety and data-race facts). Everything from the architectural flow down to memory-level execution must come from these facts, for every language, with semantics exactly per each language specification. Contract names: LangId::C, LangId::Cpp, LangId::CSharp; ASTNodeType additions NN_NAMESPACE_DECL, NN_STRUCT_DECL, NN_UNION_DECL, NN_TYPEDEF_DECL, NN_FUNCTION_DECL, NN_DESTRUCTOR_DECL, NN_OPERATOR_DECL, NN_TEMPLATE_DECL, NN_PROPERTY_DECL, NN_INDEXER_DECL, NN_EVENT_DECL, NN_DELEGATE_DECL, NN_USING_DIRECTIVE, NN_INCLUDE_DIRECTIVE, NN_GOTO_STMT, NN_LABELED_STMT, NN_FOREACH_STMT, NN_USING_STMT, NN_LOCK_STMT, NN_YIELD_STMT.
impact: Without this, OpenHeart stays Java-specific and heuristic instead of a universal, compiler-grade engine.
recommendation: Add the LangId and ASTNodeType contract variants; resolve Phase 1 and Phase 2 adapters through src/lang/registry.rs (java, kotlin, c, cpp, csharp) and delete the JavaScript-grammar fallback; upgrade tree-sitter so every grammar crate uses one compatible core version; remove Java-only assumptions from tokenization, reduction and the pipeline; make the token corpus lossless (comments, whitespace and preprocessor trivia kept with exact spans) and generate the per-grammar node-kind classification tables from the node-types.json of each grammar so no construct is ever dropped silently; make the pipeline run lowering (src/ir), memory, abi, analysis, symex, arch, memview and derive stages.

title: Succinct-tree LCA is wrong on most queries and select1 breaks on deep nesting; the tests use 3-node and 6-bit toys
evidence: rmq.rs:89-95 returns rank1(min)-1, minus 1 more if min is a close paren. For Root(A(A1,A2),B), lca(A1,B) returns A1, not Root. An exact Python port disagreed with a naive parent-walk LCA on 3,699 of 6,000 random queries. ast_tests.rs:63-79 tests only Root(C1,C2), the one shape where the formula holds, and 'Theorem 5.1' (research tests 133-135) checks only bit length. select1 (rank_select.rs:92-95) assumes which duplicate binary_search returns, which std leaves unspecified. With nesting deeper than ~1,024, Rust 1.83+ returns the last equal entry and select1(1100) = 0, not 1099. first_child and next_sibling depend on it (builder.rs:58-87).
impact: The public BPASTArtifact::lca and the 'O(1) LCA' theorem are wrong for typical ASTs. Deeply nested generated code (long else-if chains) can mis-navigate the AST and corrupt CFGs, depending on the toolchain version.
recommendation: Add proptest suites over random and path-shaped trees (up to 5,000 nodes, depth ≥ 1,100 to force all-zero superblocks). Named invariants: rank1(i) == naive popcount; select1(rank1(i)) == i on 1-bits; match_pos is an involution; lca == naive parent-walk LCA; first_child, next_sibling, subtree_size and depth agree with parent_map. Fix lca with the Navarro–Sadakane form: parent(node opening at rmq(open u, open v)+1). This passed 10,000/10,000 against the oracle. Fix select1 with partition_point(|&s| s < k) - 1.

Phase 3 always uses JavaSemanticAdapter (src/symbol/mod.rs:38) and loads only Java stubs (src/symbol/builder.rs:45; java_stubs.rs:119). The symbol model is the JVM's: SymbolVisibility{Package=0,...} (src/core/types/symbol.rs:79-80), STRICTFP and BRIDGE flags (:65,70), and a package-private default for types (src/symbol/adapter/java.rs:125-133). Call kinds mirror invokestatic/invokespecial/invokevirtual (src/cg/call_sites.rs:93-122). Allocation is recognized only as NN_NEW_EXPR (src/cg/points_to.rs:30; associations.rs:98). In src/symbol/uml_meta/associations.rs:40, stubs.contains_key("List") is always true, so every association saved in .sta is an Aggregation (the exporters ignore these records and re-join by name).
impact: Visibility, dispatch, points-to, composition and entry points are wrong or empty for non-JVM languages, and partly for Kotlin, which has no `new`. The dispatch model cannot express C++ non-virtual calls or Rust static dispatch.
recommendation: Store a lang_id on every symbol (SymbolRecord._reserved) and add a per-language LanguageSemantics profile. It covers: a visibility model mapped to UML (internal, pub(crate), fileprivate) with defaults; a dispatch policy (Joern-style STATIC/DYNAMIC plus receiver-type recovery); an allocation recognizer (a call whose callee resolves to a type); the exception model; collection types; entry points; and data-driven stubs (JDK ct.sym, typeshed, lib.d.ts). Fix associations.rs:40 to test the field's own type.

title: The generic adapter is unsound even for JavaScript, the only other real grammar
evidence: src/ingestion/adapter/generic.rs never overrides include_anonymous (default false, src/ingestion/adapter/mod.rs:14-16). As a result, src/ingestion/walker.rs:42 drops every anonymous leaf: '(', '{', ';', '=', 'class', 'import'. Pass 1 names a method by the last identifier before '(', '{' or ';' within 16 tokens (src/symbol/passes/pass1_discovery.rs:696-745), so JS methods and fields get a body identifier as their name. src/ast/adapter/generic.rs has no identifier or type_identifier arm, so there is no NN_IDENTIFIER_EXPR or NN_TYPE_REF; SSA uses (src/ssa/liveness.rs:139-161), type refs and call names are all empty. Kinds are matched by substring (:107-116) without an is_named() check, so the anonymous 'class' and 'function' keywords (:35,50) likely create nested duplicate declarations. encode_attrs returns 0 (:120-121), and a println! runs in the hot path (:26-28).
impact: JavaScript class diagrams show wrong member names and probably duplicate classes. The JS data-flow graph, call graph and type relations are empty or point back at the caller. TypeScript, Python and Rust inherit all of this through the fallback.
recommendation: Retire the generic adapter. Give each language an explicit lowering keyed on tree-sitter field names (child_by_field_name: name, body, condition, parameters, superclass) that classifies only named nodes; take names from the name field, not from token scans. Generate exhaustive match tables from each grammar's node-types.json and fail CI on any unmapped named kind. Remove the println!.

title: Position and identifier model is byte- and ASCII-based; one long line aborts Phase 1
evidence: src/ingestion/walker.rs:59 stores `col: start.column as u16`, which wraps, in the sort key's 16-bit column (src/core/types/token.rs:121-124). On a line longer than 65,535 bytes, a later token can collide with an earlier, non-adjacent one. The dedup handles only adjacent keys (src/ingestion/mod.rs:140-154), so finalize fails with 'Invariant 2 Violation' (src/ingestion/builder.rs:49-56). The server collects .js files from everywhere except a few directory names (src/adapters/server.rs:764-866), for example a committed javadoc jquery-*.min.js. src/ast/reducer.rs:56 saturates the column instead of wrapping it. Sources are parsed as raw bytes with no BOM or charset handling. Identifier checks need an ASCII first byte (pass1_discovery.rs:687,714,766,803), and class_diagram.rs:98-101 rejects non-ASCII and '$' names.
impact: One minified or generated file aborts the server's analysis of a whole repository. Unicode identifiers (legal in Java, Kotlin, Python, JS, Rust and Swift) and '$' names disappear. Columns are UTF-8 bytes, not the UTF-16 units editors use.
recommendation: Anchor tokens on u32 byte offsets and derive line/col lazily from a line index. If the packed key stays, widen columns to u32 and break ties globally by token_id. Skip and report minified or generated files using linguist-style rules (line length, .min.js, generated-file headers). Transcode non-UTF-8 input (BOM sniffing, encoding_rs), use Unicode XID rules (unicode-ident crate) for identifiers, and expose UTF-16 columns to the web studio and LSP clients.

title: No entry definitions for parameters, this, captured variables or fields
evidence: Parameters are NN_PARAM_DECL children of the declaration and are never placed in a block. ENTRY is empty, and rename_dfs starts from an empty VersionStack. Uses with no reaching def are silently dropped (`current_ver != u32::MAX`), and φ args get u32::MAX. SSA_FLAG_IS_PARAM_DEF, IS_FIELD_DEF, IS_RETURN_VAL and IS_CONST are never set anywhere.
impact: Parameter-to-use flows, which taint and null analyses need, cannot exist even after FLOW-04 is fixed.
recommendation: Emit version-0 defs in ENTRY for each parameter, `this` and captured variables (optionally fields too), with the flags set. Use an explicit undefined version instead of u32::MAX, and count undefined uses.

title: TH_EXTENDS vs TH_IMPLEMENTS is guessed from the target's kind, so implements clauses become extends edges
evidence: The AST eliminates the superclass and super_interfaces nodes, so Pass 5 sees bare TYPE_REFs and only emits IMPLEMENTS for class-to-interface pairs. Enums and records implementing interfaces, and classes implementing external interfaces such as Runnable or Serializable, get EXTENDS. The test sample `extends BaseService implements Runnable` produces two EXTENDS edges, and class_diagram keeps the last one, so the superclass shown is Runnable. Lines 64-67 duplicate the else branch, and target kinds are never checked.
impact: Class diagrams show the wrong superclass and apparent multiple inheritance; enums and records lose their realization edges.
recommendation: Keep the clause information: retain the superclass and super_interfaces nodes or tag their TYPE_REFs in NodeAttr, and derive the relation from syntax. In the token scan, use the keyword actually seen. Reject targets that are not type kinds. Add tests for enum, record and external-interface cases.

title: variable_declarator becomes its own SK_LOCAL_VAR, duplicating fields and locals and losing all but one field of `int a, b;`
evidence: A field_declaration yields one SK_FIELD, and each child variable_declarator yields an SK_LOCAL_VAR under it. `private int a, b;` gives a single SK_FIELD named "b" plus locals "a" and "b", so field a never exists. Every local yields two SK_LOCAL_VARs. Declarator symbols are never typed because the type node is a sibling, not a child. This is about symbol count and kind, not the naming problem in SYM-02.
impact: Fields from multi-declarator statements vanish from class diagrams, and SSA and points-to see doubled, untyped locals.
recommendation: Treat each variable_declarator as the declaration: emit one SK_FIELD or SK_LOCAL_VAR per declarator, taking kind and type from the enclosing declaration, and emit no symbol for the wrapper. Test that `int a, b;` produces two SK_FIELD symbols typed int.

title: Constructor bodies, switch blocks and annotation bodies are dropped before Phase 3, so declarations inside them never become symbols
evidence: The reducer's catch-all `_ => Drop` discards any unlisted node kind together with its subtree. tree-sitter-java 0.20.2 wraps constructor bodies in constructor_body, switch bodies in switch_block and annotation members in annotation_type_body, and none of these is mapped. Locals, lambdas and classes in constructors and switches never reach Pass 1, constructor token ranges stop at the parameter list, and has_new_expr_in_subtree can never find a `new`. SYM-12's list does not include these.
impact: Every constructor looks empty to Phase 3, and composition detection stays impossible even after SYM-08 is fixed.
recommendation: Map constructor_body to NN_BLOCK, and map switch_block, switch_rule and annotation_type_body to Eliminate or to kept nodes. Add a Phase 3 test asserting that a local declared in a constructor becomes an SK_LOCAL_VAR under that constructor.

title: Java reducer emits every variable_declarator as a second NN_LOCAL_VAR_DECL, duplicating declarations
evidence: java.rs:42 maps both local_variable_declaration and variable_declarator to Keep(NN_LOCAL_VAR_DECL). Declarators are children of field and local declarations, so `private int x = 1;` becomes FIELD_DECL[TYPE_REF, LOCAL_VAR_DECL[x, 1]] and `int a = 1;` nests two LOCAL_VAR_DECLs. Pass 1 creates a symbol for each such node, and create_symbol does no dedup.
impact: Every field gains a phantom SK_LOCAL_VAR child and every local is declared twice. Symbol counts, scopes and def/use attribution are skewed.
recommendation: Add a distinct NN_VAR_DECLARATOR kind, or Eliminate declarators and emit one decl node per declared name with the shared type. Make discovery create exactly one symbol per name, and add a golden test asserting one symbol for `int a = 1;`.

title: Enum constants are dropped from the AST, so SK_ENUM_CONSTANT is never produced
evidence: enum_body and enum_body_declarations are Eliminate, but enum_constant has no arm and falls to `_ => Drop` (java.rs:129), discarding the constant, its arguments and any constant body. ASTNodeType has no enum-constant kind. grep finds nothing that creates SK_ENUM_CONSTANT, although class_diagram.rs:209 and tra/builder.rs:84 consume it.
impact: Enums appear in UML and traceability with no literals. Constant arguments and constant-specific bodies are missing from the CFG, SSA and call graph.
recommendation: Add NN_ENUM_CONSTANT to ASTNodeType. Keep enum_constant with its name, argument_list and class_body, map it to SK_ENUM_CONSTANT in the semantic adapter, and add an enum golden test.

title: The BP AST stores no child roles, so consumers decode children by position and misread for and enhanced-for loops
evidence: PreorderArrays hold only type, attr, range and parent. Tree-sitter field names are discarded and NN_ELSE_CLAUSE is never emitted. `for (String s : list) {...}` yields [TYPE_REF, s, list, BLOCK], yet for_stmt.rs:88-101 takes the third child (`list`) as the body. In for_stmt.rs:26-35, `for (; i<n; i++)` and two-variable inits shift the init/cond/update/body positions.
impact: CFGs for common loops lose the real loop body or treat updates as conditions. A dropped then-branch moves the else branch into the then position.
recommendation: Persist a per-node role byte (the tree-sitter field id) in PreorderArrays and in the .bpa. Emit NN_ELSE_CLAUSE or placeholder nodes for omitted parts, and expose child_by_role accessors for the CFG builders.

title: Java reducer silently drops many constructs beyond those in CORE-02
evidence: Through `_ => Drop`, these tree-sitter-java 0.20 kinds vanish: package, import and module declarations, constant_declaration (interface fields), annotation_type_body, catch_formal_parameter, inferred_parameters, explicit_constructor_invocation, yield_statement, scoped_type_identifier, array_type, class_literal, dimensions_expr, throws, permits, annotation_argument_list, octal_integer_literal and hex_floating_point_literal. CORE-02 covers only constructor bodies, switch bodies, try-with-resources and generic types.
impact: Qualified supertypes, array parameter types, catch types, interface constants, lambda parameters and some operands disappear, so symbols, types and data flow are wrong.
recommendation: Make the default arm Eliminate, or at least log unmapped kinds. Add node types for imports, packages, catch parameters, class literals and qualified or array types. Add a test that walks node-types.json and fails on any unclassified named kind.

title: LabelExtractor slices UTF-8 labels by byte and panics on non-ASCII tokens, aborting Phase 9
evidence: `&label_text[..max_chars.saturating_sub(3)]` slices by byte length. It runs for every non-entry/exit block (max 30). node_attr is misused as a token index, so it reads token 0 or op<<12 (e.g. token #86016 for `==` conditions). A token such as 'Bitte geben Sie Ihr Passwört ein', or CJK text, puts byte 27 in the middle of a character (checked in Python), so the slice panics.
impact: Phase 9 crashes on such input. The single-threaded server has no catch_unwind, so a crafted repo sent to /api/analyze is a remote DoS.
recommendation: Truncate on char boundaries (char_indices().nth(n)) and never byte-slice a String. Add test_extract_label_multibyte_truncation with umlaut and CJK tokens. This differs from UML-12, which is about reading the wrong token.

title: A panic in any request or phase kills the server process
evidence: start() calls handle_connection on the main thread (server.rs:40-42) with no catch_unwind and no worker thread. Phases 1-9 run inline (server.rs:527-617) and contain asserts and unchecked slicing (src/ast/builder.rs:180, src/ast/mod.rs:58-59). run.sh launches a dev build, where debug_assert! is active (token.rs:122).
impact: One unusual or crafted repository terminates the service for everyone and leaves temp dirs behind.
recommendation: Run each request on a worker thread, or wrap it in catch_unwind with AssertUnwindSafe. Turn panics into logged 500 responses and keep accepting. Test: a handler that panics returns 500 and the next request succeeds.

title: Symlinked source files are read through to devices and host files
evidence: collect_files keeps any entry with a code extension without checking that it is a regular file (server.rs:805-884), and ingestion follows the link in fs::metadata/fs::read (src/ingestion/mod.rs:51-54). A cloned Evil.java -> /dev/zero grows memory until OOM. X.java -> /etc/... pulls host files into results and, via walkdir_find, into /api/source. The CLI has the same gap (main.rs:90-95).
impact: One public repository can crash the server with OOM or expose host files through analysis output.
recommendation: Accept only regular files using DirEntry::file_type() without following links, or canonicalize and require targets inside the repo. Cap per-file size before reading. Test: a symlink to /dev/zero is skipped.

title: Unbounded recursion on the 1 MB main thread: deep CST, CFG, dominator, BDD or call-graph inputs abort the process
evidence: Recursion depth grows with the input in: ingestion/walker.rs:32-71 and ast/reducer.rs:8-68 (CST depth; long + chains and else-if chains nest one level per term); cfg/stmts/if_stmt.rs:34,49; rpo.rs:7, loops.rs:29, postdom.rs:24 and ssa/cdg.rs:37 (DFS depth ≈ block count); ssa/renaming.rs:103-192 (dominator-tree depth, 12-argument frames); liveness.rs:165; bdd/apply.rs:103-104,137-138 and sat_count.rs:79 (≈ variable count); cg/scc.rs:63-85 (Tarjan). Everything runs on the main thread (main.rs, server.rs:40-41), whose default stack is 1 MB on Windows/MSVC and 8 MB on Linux.
impact: A stack overflow aborts the process rather than panicking. The CLI or the HTTP server dies on one deep generated file (JFlex/ANTLR output, huge initializers) with no partial output, and an attacker can kill the server through /api/analyze.
recommendation: Convert these routines to explicit-stack iteration: TreeCursor goto_first_child/goto_next_sibling/goto_parent loops, (node, child_idx) DFS frames, Pearce's iterative SCC (petgraph::algo::tarjan_scc), and an iterative apply with an ITE cache. As a stopgap, run the pipeline on std::thread::Builder::new().stack_size(512<<20). Add stress tests: a 100K-term concatenation, a 20K-branch else-if chain and a 50K-block method.

title: Fixed-width ids overflow at scale: u16 file ids, u8 block ids, u16 counts
evidence: ingestion/mod.rs:70,123 cast file_id with `as u16`, and token.rs:121 packs 16-bit file ids into sort keys. File 65,536 wraps onto file 0, and the key collisions trip Invariant 2 (ingestion/builder.rs:52), which aborts Phase 1. core/types/ssa.rs:25,43 stores def_block as (def_block & 0xFF) as u8, so the global block offsets in tra/backward/ssa_bi.rs:17-35 are wrong for every function after one with more than 256 blocks. Also truncated: SCC size as u16 (cg/scc.rs:38), orig_sym_id & 0xFFFF on disk (ssa/serializer.rs:113), line numbers as u16 (sym_span.rs:38-40), UMA counts as u16 (sequence_diagram.rs:158).
impact: Phase 1 fails outright beyond 65,535 files (monorepos such as intellij-community with testData), and traceability and artifacts are silently corrupted on ordinary large code (methods over 256 blocks, files over 65,535 lines).
recommendation: Widen ids, counts and line numbers to u32, and split sort_key into (file_id: u32, byte_offset: u32) or a u128. Replace every `as uN` on a length with uN::try_from(..)? returning a typed error. Add generated tests: 70K files, 300-block methods, 70K-line files, and .ssa/.uma round-trips.

title: The 'succinct' AST costs about 210–236 B/node, roughly 45× the documented 4.65 B, and select1 scans bit by bit
evidence: ast/rmq.rs:24-51 builds a full sparse table (Vec<Vec<u32>>, log n levels over 2N bits) plus excess as Vec<i32> and log2 as Vec<usize>. jump_table.rs:16 stores one u32 per bit, and the preorder arrays add 17 B/node. A model of these formulas (scratchpad lens/scale_model.py) gives 209 B/node at 1M nodes and 1.09 GiB at 5M nodes (≈1M LOC), of which 852 MiB is the RMQ table. serializer.rs:183-184 rebuilds the table on every read, and rank_select.rs:100 implements select1 as a get_bit loop. docs/overview.md:119 and architecture.md:107 claim 4.65 MB per 1M nodes.
impact: The AST alone exceeds 1 GB at 1M LOC. Every first_child/next_sibling call (10^7–10^8 calls across Phases 3–6) costs hundreds of cycles. The README's 128× compression and O(1) navigation claims are contradicted.
recommendation: Add a subtree_size (or close-position-by-preorder) array beside parent_map so navigation is O(1) without select. Replace the sparse table with a Navarro–Sadakane range-min-max tree, or Fischer–Heun block RMQ in 2n+o(n) bits. Use Rank9/Select9 or Elias–Fano from the sucds or vers-vecs crates. Publish B/node figures measured with dhat or peak-RSS benchmarks.

title: Single-threaded pipeline that reads every file three times and parses it twice
evidence: Cargo.toml has no rayon or any other parallelism crate, and core/pipeline.rs:170-225 and main.rs:150-254 run the phases strictly serially. Phase 1 reads each file twice (ingestion/mod.rs:53, 111) and parses it with a single Parser (108); the Mutex-wrapped interner (105) is never shared across threads. Phase 2 re-reads and re-parses every file (ast/mod.rs:142-143). Kotlin is parsed with the Java grammar (kotlin.rs:30) and then with the JavaScript fallback, because no Kotlin AST adapter is registered (ast/adapter/registry.rs:19-28). Phases 4, 5, 8 and 9 loop over functions serially.
impact: Uses one core and pays twice the front-end parse cost. Kotlin-heavy repos pay wrong-grammar error recovery twice. About 8–12× of the available throughput on 16 cores goes unused.
recommendation: Parse once and emit tokens plus the reduced BP AST in the same walk. Run rayon par_iter over files with a per-thread tree_sitter::Parser (map_init), discover files with the ignore or jwalk crate, and merge per-file interners (or use lasso::ThreadedRodeo). Assign token ids from per-file counts plus a prefix sum. Use par_iter over functions in Phases 4, 5 and 8 and over classes in Phase 9; ruff and Biome use this per-file model.

title: No two runs produce identical artifacts or diagrams: timestamps, mtimes, HashMap order and raw path strings leak into outputs
evidence: .tca embeds SystemTime::now() and per-file mtimes (ingestion/serializer.rs:80-84,115; ingestion/mod.rs:62-67). .bpa embeds the .tca CRC (ast/serializer.rs:31), so every later link hash changes on each run. .sta serializes two HashMaps in iteration order (symbol/serializer.rs:169,180). .scpg embeds a timestamp (scpg/serializer/mod.rs:136-140). The TRA hash is taken over Debug output that includes mtimes (hash_chain.rs:36). Iteration order also leaks: HashSet-to-Vec relations (class_diagram.rs:300-301), lifelines via into_values (sequence_diagram.rs:153), JSON packages, edges and edge ids (json.rs:148,445,518), call-graph edges in HashSet order (plantuml.rs:1432; mermaid.rs:1605), and phi order (placement.rs:37). Invocation path strings are stored verbatim (ingestion/mod.rs:137-138).
impact: Results cannot be reproduced or diffed, golden tests are impossible, the committed web/diagrams change on every run, and all UMLLinks look stale after a rebuild. README's 'deterministically derives' claim is false.
recommendation: Use BTreeMap or IndexMap, or sort, before every serialization and export. Drop wall-clock timestamps from artifacts (or honour SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH) and keep mtimes out of hashes. Store root-relative POSIX paths (camino, path-slash). Add a CI job that runs analyze twice, once from another working directory and with shuffled discovery order, and requires byte-identical outputs (cmp or diffoscope, as reproducible-builds.org recommends).

title: Four separate pipelines (CLI, server, test builder, browser) give different results for the same repository
evidence: The CLI analyzes .java/.kt/.kts files, tests included (main.rs:76-99). The server takes 58 extensions and drops test and build dirs and *Test files (server.rs:770-884). It never calls Phase10Stage yet reports 'All 10 phases verified' (server.rs:619-699), and it swallows IO errors with unwrap_or_default (server.rs:536-609). It ignores the client's diagram_types (api.js:36 vs server.rs:366-372) and writes into the git-tracked web/diagrams shared by every session (server.rs:636-691). SCPGPipelineBuilder, the only path the tests use, writes graph.scpg instead of unified.scpg and ignores diagram_formats (pipeline.rs:100,143-148,168). The browser engine regex-parses only the first 30 files and uses a random compiler_hash (github-engine.js:102,576). The Dockerfile runs `openheart serve`, which main.rs rejects (main.rs:532,544; Dockerfile:49).
impact: The same repository gives different classes and diagrams depending on entry point. Tests and the F1 harness validate paths the CLI does not run. Concurrent sessions overwrite each other's diagrams, and the Docker image exits at startup.
recommendation: Expose one library entry point, Pipeline::run(&AnalysisConfig) -> Result<AnalysisOutputs, PipelineError>, with include/exclude globs, languages and formats. Call it from the CLI, the server and the tests, and delete the copies. Have the server write per-session directories served under /sessions/{id}/ and never touch web/. Add a contract test asserting byte-identical CLI and server outputs for a fixture, fix the Dockerfile CMD, and regenerate the Pages demo from the engine in CI.

title: Error handling is inconsistent across phases: global aborts on local faults, silent skips, panics, and invariants met by editing data
evidence: One unreadable file or a None parse aborts Phase 1 (ingestion/mod.rs:51-54,111,117), and one odd function aborts Phases 4 and 5 (cfg/mod.rs:84; ssa/mod.rs:81). Yet Phase 2 silently skips files it cannot read or parse (ast/mod.rs:141-154). Phases 7-10 return no Result and panic or assert instead (tra/mod.rs:42-44; tra/builder.rs:67-130; psa/mod.rs:153-155; uma/mod.rs:97-99; scpg/mod.rs:53-55). The single-threaded server has no catch_unwind (server.rs:40-42). Invariants are met by editing data: empty blocks map to token 0 (blk_bi.rs:17-21), orphans are moved under symbol 0 (pass1_discovery.rs:622-627), and hierarchy cycles are deleted (pass5_hierarchy.rs:218). thiserror is a dependency but is never used, and error JSON interpolates Debug paths (server.rs:530-533).
impact: Large repositories fail completely on one bad unit, or degrade silently. One panic stops the server for every user, and real resolution bugs stay hidden. The CLI prints 'SYSTEM PRODUCTION READY' even when diagram writes fail (main.rs:289-341).
recommendation: Define a StageError enum with thiserror. Make every stage return Result and record per-file Diagnostics (file, phase, kind, message) in a diagnostics table, as CodeQL extractors do, continuing past local faults. Turn invariant checks into reported errors, never data patches. Run each server request under catch_unwind or in a worker pool, and build every response with serde_json. When a run is degraded, exit non-zero and report the skipped files and failed functions.

title: Byte-index slicing in LabelExtractor panics on non-ASCII text, and labels come from the wrong token
evidence: extract_label truncates with `&label_text[..max_chars.saturating_sub(3)]` (label_extraction.rs:33-35). activity_diagram.rs:89 passes 30, so byte 27 must fall on a char boundary. The text is token_records[bpa.node_attr(stmt)] (line 23), but node_attr is the packed visibility/modifier/operator word (java.rs:177, ast.rs:209-213), which is 0 for expression and return statements. As a result, nearly every block label is token 0 of the whole corpus. If token 0 is at least 28 bytes with a multi-byte char spanning byte 27, Phase 9 panics with 'byte index 27 is not a char boundary'. Examples: the first file starts with an identifier of 16 'ç' characters, or with Cyrillic or CJK text.
impact: A deterministic Phase 9 panic. It is rare in Java-only CLI runs (token 0 is usually `package`), plausible for non-English Python/JS files ingested by the server, and trivially crafted: a one-file repository sent to /api/analyze kills the server. Every activity label is also wrong.
recommendation: Truncate on char boundaries (`s.char_indices().nth(n)`, str::floor_char_boundary once stable, or unicode-segmentation for graphemes), and ban raw string slicing with clippy::string_slice. Derive labels from bpa.token_range(stmt).0 instead of node_attr. Add proptest and fuzz corpora with Unicode identifiers (legal in both Java and Kotlin) and CJK or emoji literals.

title: 16-bit column in sort keys: one line longer than 64 KB aborts the whole repository run
evidence: walker.rs:59 stores `col: start.column as u16`, which wraps. build_sort_key packs file (u16), line (u24) and col (u16) into one key (token.rs:121-124), and the duplicate counter only separates consecutive equal keys (ingestion/mod.rs:140-155). Two tokens on one line at columns c and c+65,536 therefore get the same key, and finalize returns 'Invariant 2 Violation (Injectivity)' (builder.rs:49-55). A port of this logic finds 2,232 duplicate keys in a single 70 KB line. The server also ingests .js files (server.rs:816), so a committed jquery.min.js under src/main/resources/static fails the analysis, and long generated Java/Kotlin lines do the same. reducer.rs:56 clamps the column instead of wrapping it, so Phase 2 lookups disagree with Phase 1.
impact: A single minified or generated file makes the entire run fail with no partial output. A file with more than 16,777,215 lines (line & 0xFFFFFF) has the same effect.
recommendation: Identify tokens by (file_id u32, byte_offset) or by a per-file ordinal, and keep line and column in separate u32 tables, as tree-sitter's Point does. If packing stays, saturate and flag instead of wrapping. Turn the injectivity check into a per-file diagnostic that skips the offending file rather than failing the run. Add boundary tests: a 70 KB line, a 16.8M-line file, and minified JS.

title: Packed u8/u16 fields silently truncate at realistic sizes, corrupting SSA, PSA, traceability and UMA data
evidence: With overflow checks off, narrowing casts wrap silently. SSARecord.def_block is a u8 (core/types/ssa.rs:25,43), so block numbers of 256 and above alias. feasibility.rs:115-119 then matches on `block_id & 0xFF`, and ssa_bi.rs:17-35 builds global block offsets from the truncated maxima, which shifts every later function. Span lines are cast `as u16` (sym_span.rs:38-40, cs_span.rs:32), and so is file_id (ingestion/mod.rs:70,123). PSA maps edges beyond 65,535 to var 0 (psa/ordering/mod.rs:40-55), and its condition variables are ssa_id&0x3FFF, which collide with edge variables (feasibility.rs:122). SCC sizes, UMA counts and token lengths are also cast `as u16` (cg/scc.rs:38, uma/serializer.rs:39-40, walker.rs:54, interner.rs:99).
impact: SSA, path-count, traceability and UML data come out wrong, with no error, for methods over 256 blocks, files over 65,535 lines and repositories over 65,535 files. Those are exactly the inputs a benchmark contains.
recommendation: Widen on-disk fields to u32 (or LEB128 varints) behind a format-version bump. Replace every narrowing `as` with u16::try_from mapped to a typed error, or to an explicit saturate-and-diagnose. Deny clippy::cast_possible_truncation. Give BDD condition variables their own index space. Add CI boundary tests: a 257-block method, a 65,536-line file, 65,536 synthetic files and a 70 KB token.

title: Unbounded native recursion on input-controlled depth causes stack-overflow aborts that cannot be caught
evidence: Recursion depth follows the input in at least eleven places with no limit: CST walks (walker.rs:32-77, reducer.rs:8-93), statement nesting including else-if chains (cfg/stmts/mod.rs:28-65), expression trees (liveness.rs:124-169), block-graph DFS (rpo.rs:7-17, loops.rs:29-46, postdom.rs:24-33, cdg.rs:37-48), dominator-tree renaming (renaming.rs:103-211), Tarjan over the call graph (cg/scc.rs:63-105), and BDD apply (depth equals n_vars). classify() receives the current depth but ignores it (java.rs:26). A left-associative concatenation of N literals has CST depth of about N. Everything runs on the main thread, which has a 1 MiB stack with MSVC on Windows and 8 MiB on Linux.
impact: Generated code with thousands of concatenated literals, long else-if chains, huge straight-line methods or deep call chains aborts the CLI or the server. On Windows a few thousand levels likely suffice (frame sizes are estimates).
recommendation: Make tree walks iterative using TreeCursor (goto_first_child, goto_next_sibling, goto_parent) or explicit stacks. Use iterative Tarjan (Pearce 2016) and iterative DFS for RPO and SSA renaming. Wrap any remaining recursion in stacker::maybe_grow, as rustc's ensure_sufficient_stack does. Run the pipeline on a thread with an explicit large stack, and enforce a nesting limit that emits a diagnostic. Add tests with 100,000-level nesting to CI on both Windows and Linux.

title: select1 returns the root when a superblock has no 1-bits, corrupting AST navigation on long else-if chains
evidence: select1 (rank_select.rs:86-108) binary-searches the cumulative superblocks array for target_rank and starts scanning at idx-1. When a 512-bit superblock holds only close parens (512 or more consecutive closes, such as the tail of a long else-if chain), adjacent entries are equal. Rust's binary_search then returns the last equal index, the scan starts after the target, and the function returns 0. A port of build/select1 run on an else-if model produces a wrong answer from about 400 branches, depending on alignment. first_child() (builder.rs:58-66) then reports node 1 as a child of that leaf, so walkers such as extract_stmt_vars (liveness.rs:162-169) can re-enter the root subtree without bound.
impact: Generated dispatch code gets wrong first_child, next_sibling, depth and LCA answers, and therefore wrong CFG and SSA facts. In the plausible worst case the recursion is unbounded and ends in a stack-overflow abort.
recommendation: Choose the superblock with `superblocks.partition_point(|&c| c < target) - 1`, or adopt a tested implementation (sucds, vers-vecs, or rank9/select9 from Vigna 2008). Add proptest checks that compare rank1, select1, first_child and next_sibling against a naive pointer tree, on random BP strings and on adversarial long runs of opens and closes.

title: Source discovery follows symlinks with no cycle, file-type or root checks, and one bad file aborts the run
evidence: collect_source_files (main.rs:84-96), collect_files (server.rs:764-804) and walkdir_find (server.rs:342-361) recurse whenever Path::is_dir() is true, and is_dir() follows symlinks. None of them keeps a visited set, caps depth or confines paths to the repository root. A cloned repo containing `a -> .` and `b -> .` makes traversal exponential. `Big.java -> /dev/zero` passes the extension filter, and fs::read (ingestion/mod.rs:53) reads until memory runs out. `x -> /` ingests the host filesystem. Per-file failures are fatal: a dangling symlink fails fs::metadata (ingestion/mod.rs:51-52), and the CLI's `?` (main.rs:85-86) turns one ENAMETOOLONG from a self-link into 'Failed to scan directory'.
impact: Malicious repositories, and merely messy ones (dangling links are common), hang the run, exhaust memory or abort the whole analysis. The server can also be steered into reading outside the clone.
recommendation: Use the ignore crate (ripgrep's walker) with follow_links(false), same_file_system(true), max_depth and .gitignore support. Accept only entries where symlink_metadata() reports a regular file and the canonicalized path lies under the repository root. Cap per-file size (configurable, e.g. 8 MiB) with File::take. Record per-file errors as diagnostics and continue, as ruff and rust-analyzer do.

title: Artifacts are non-deterministic (wall-clock time, file mtimes, raw paths), so the hash chain changes on every run
evidence: The .tca header embeds SystemTime::now() (ingestion/serializer.rs:80-84), each file's mtime_ns (ingestion/mod.rs:62-67, written at serializer.rs:115) and paths exactly as passed in. Phase 2 hashes the whole .tca (ast/mod.rs:48) and each later phase chains on upstream bytes. As a result, identical source yields different hashes in all ten artifacts on every run, and so does a git checkout that only touches mtimes. The .scpg header adds now_ns and writes source_hash as zeros (scpg/serializer/mod.rs:136-146). The published demo diagrams are whatever the last local server run wrote into web/diagrams (server.rs:637).
impact: Staleness and incremental detection (the paper's Eq. 8, 'O(1) invalidation') can never report 'unchanged'. Byte-level golden tests, build caching and cross-machine reproduction of benchmark artifacts are all impossible.
recommendation: Make serialization a pure function of content. Drop wall-clock time and mtimes from hashed bytes; if needed, keep them in an unhashed sidecar that honours SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH. Store project-relative paths normalized to '/', and chain on content digests (BLAKE3 or SHA-256 over canonical sections) rather than whole-file CRCs. Generate demo diagrams in CI from a pinned input. Add a CI job that runs the pipeline twice, on two OSes, and byte-compares every artifact, as reproducible-builds.org recommends.

title: No error model: String errors, an unused thiserror, panics in Phases 7-9, silently dropped files and integer truncation
evidence: thiserror is declared (Cargo.toml:13) but never used, and src has no error enum. 27 signatures return Result<_, String>, and callers re-stringify errors with {:?}. Phases 7-9 return bare artifacts and panic! when a write fails (tra/mod.rs:43, psa/mod.rs:154, uma/mod.rs:98). Phase 2 silently skips any file it cannot read or parse (nested `if let Ok`, ast/mod.rs:140-152). The server hashes `fs::read(..).unwrap_or_default()` (server.rs:536-609). `file_id as u16` (ingestion/mod.rs:70) wraps past 65,536 files and `column as u16` (walker.rs:59) past column 65,535, although security-architecture.md:26 claims these values saturate. 291 unwraps remain.
impact: A full disk or a permission error aborts the server. Unreadable files vanish from the results with no warning. Large monorepos and minified files get colliding sort keys and wrong traceability, all silently.
recommendation: Define typed errors per layer with thiserror, for example ArtifactError {Truncated, BadMagic, CrcMismatch{expected, found}, Version} and IngestError {Io{path}, Parse{path}}, and use anyhow or miette only in the CLI. Make every stage return Result, and record per-file diagnostics instead of skipping files. Replace `as` casts with u16::try_from plus explicit errors, or widen the IDs. Deny clippy::unwrap_used, expect_used, panic and indexing_slicing in library code, following the Rust API Guidelines (C-GOOD-ERR).

title: No language-neutral IR: a Java-shaped AST with no node roles is the contract for every phase
evidence: ASTNodeType (src/core/types/ast.rs:6-68) is about 52 Java constructs (NN_INSTANCEOF_EXPR, NN_METHOD_REF, NN_RECORD_DECL). It has no kinds for imports or namespaces, free functions, decorators, with/defer, match arms, await or comprehensions. The 'Language Specific (Java Extensions)' range 0x80-0x84 (:62-67) is not namespaced, and nodes store no language id (src/ast/builder.rs:147-161). Tree-sitter field roles are discarded, so CFG lowering guesses each child's role from the number of children (src/cfg/stmts/for_stmt.rs:117-127). For Java `for (; i < n; )`, the condition is taken as the initializer and no exit edge is added (:167-169). unpack_operator_id returns Assign for every operator (src/core/types/ast.rs:224-232).
impact: Every language has to pretend to be Java. Constructs with no Java equivalent are dropped or lowered wrongly, and guessing roles by position breaks even Java. This is the root cause of LANG-01 through LANG-06.
recommendation: Add a Unified IR between the parse tree and Phase 3. It needs a closed core set of node kinds (Module, TypeDecl{class|interface|trait|struct|enum|record|object}, Function{method|ctor|async|generator}, Loop{kind}, Match, Try, With, Call{dispatch}, Alloc, Member, Name, Import). Each node carries a role byte (cond, then, else, init, update, body, callee, receiver, arg, name, type, super), a full operator id and a (lang, kind) extension pair, plus a file-to-language table. Lower per language as Joern's x2cpg frontends and Semgrep's AST_generic-to-IL do. Share CFG/SSA/dataflow code across languages through a language signature, as CodeQL's shared libraries do. Migration: .bpa v2 with roles, lower Java first and switch CFG/SSA to roles; then add Kotlin/Python/TS frontends; finally delete the token heuristics.

title: Integrity checks are untested and partly fake: 'VERIFIED VALID' without a CRC, a non-standard PSA CRC, a count-based hash chain
evidence: cmd_inspect prints 'CRC-64 Check : VERIFIED VALID' for .tca and .bpa after matching only the magic number (main.rs:373-388). psa::crc64_ecma (psa/serializer.rs:259-279) yields 0xD428DA62D41203D6 for '123456789', while the catalogue CRC-64/ECMA-182 value, which ingestion's copy matches, is 0x6C40DF5F0B497347. Its doc claim to match the other serializers is therefore false, and its only test checks determinism (334-340). ScpgHashChain hashes the file count as 'bpa_hash', call_site_count as 'cga_hash', and a Debug string that includes mtime_ns (hash_chain.rs:36-41). The only test asserts scpg_hash != 0. No test flips a byte.
impact: Corrupt .tca and .bpa files are reported as valid, and standard tools cannot verify .psa checksums. Staleness detection misses content edits that keep the counts equal, and fires on a mere touch.
recommendation: Consolidate into one checksum module with known-answer tests against the crc crate's CRC_64_ECMA_182. For every artifact, add a proptest that flips a random bit in the serialized file and asserts read() returns Err, and make inspect call the real readers. Add metamorphic staleness tests: editing a method body while keeping counts equal must change scpg_hash, and touching files or re-checking out without edits must not. Derive the component hashes from artifact bytes.

title: Artifact loaders and the request parser are unfuzzed; malformed files with a valid CRC panic or abort
evidence: The BPA reader trusts on-disk lengths. `Vec::with_capacity(words_len)` with values up to 2^32 aborts on allocation, and `buf[offset..offset+8]` panics on a short payload. bit_count is never checked against words.len(), so get_bit indexes out of bounds inside RankSelectIndex::build (ast/serializer.rs:109-127, 183). MemoryMappedSCPG::open size-checks for 11 sections but then loops over the file's own section_count (mmap/mod.rs:19-72). get_section adds offset and length without overflow checks (81-93). The serializers contain about 270 unwrap/expect calls, and there is no fuzz/ directory.
impact: Truncated, hostile or version-skewed artifacts crash the CLI and engine instead of returning errors, and loader panics stay invisible until a user hits them.
recommendation: Add a cargo-fuzz target per loader (tca, bpa, sta, cfa, ssa, cga, tra, psa, uma, scpg), with a harness that recomputes the trailing CRC so mutated inputs pass the checksum gate. Add structured `arbitrary` round-trip targets asserting read(write(x)) == x, a target that feeds raw source bytes through the whole pipeline, and an HTTP-parser target. Seed corpora from test outputs, run 10 minutes nightly, and apply to OSS-Fuzz. Use a bounds-checked BinaryReader that returns Err.

title: The adapter and registry design forces 25+ file edits per new language
evidence: Two language-id registries disagree: src/ingestion/adapter/registry.rs:19-42 has Kotlin, while src/ast/adapter/registry.rs:16-31 has TS/Rust/Generic. `ext_map` is written but never read (registry.rs:46-48); detect() is a separate hardcoded match (:59-83). File selection differs yet again in src/main.rs:79-93, src/adapters/server.rs:790-881 (which drops '*test' stems such as Latest.java and any /spec package), web/js/github-engine.js:89 and ruthless_config.json. Each file is parsed twice, and Phase 2 re-reads it from disk without checking the stored SHA-256 (src/ast/mod.rs:142). PatternDetectionChain and SCPGPipelineBuilder are used only by tests, and the pipeline is copied by hand (main.rs:150-255, server.rs:526-620). tree-sitter is pinned to 0.20 (Cargo.toml:8).
impact: Adding Python today touches 25+ files across all ten phases: Cargo.toml, both registries, the core type enums, the symbol adapter, stubs and passes 1-5, cfg/stmts, ssa/liveness, cg, uma, four exporters, main.rs, server.rs, the tests, the verifier and the web engine.
recommendation: Make one LanguageFrontend trait and registry the single source of truth. It defines: id; dialects (ts/tsx, kts); extensions plus shebang or linguist-style detection; grammar; token classifier; lowering to the IR; LanguageSemantics; name-binding rules (TSG); and stub data. Parse each file once and hand the tree to Phase 2. Drive the CLI, the server, /api/supported-languages and the verifier from the registry, and run every entry point through SCPGPipelineBuilder. Upgrade to tree-sitter 0.25 (LanguageFn). Done = adding a language means one module plus fixtures.

title: φ operands are recorded as anonymous u32::MAX uses in the def-use CSR
evidence: When rename_dfs fills φ arguments, it pushes u32::MAX into the reaching def's use list instead of the φ's ssa_id or block, and stores arg_ssa_id = u32::MAX when no def reaches. Ordinary uses store the statement node, repeated once per occurrence. DefUseCSR documents none of these conventions.
impact: Def-use walks cannot continue through φ-functions, and every consumer has to special-case the sentinels.
recommendation: Record φ uses as the φ's ssa_id (or as a tagged entry), dedupe per statement, use an explicit undefined def, and document what use_adj contains.

title: Switch case-label detection marks every case group as default
evidence: build_switch counts a group as labelled only when its first child is NN_LITERAL or NN_IDENTIFIER_EXPR. The Java reducer drops switch_label (unlisted kind, `_ => Drop`), so the first child is a statement and has_default is set for every group. Qualified constants such as Color.RED, constant expressions and patterns would also be read as default. Labels are never recorded.
impact: After FLOW-02's body loss is fixed, switches without a default still lose their selector-to-exit edge, and case values are gone.
recommendation: Keep switch_label (and switch_rule) in the adapter, detect `default` explicitly, record every label of a group on the Switch edge, and suppress fall-through for arrow rules. This differs from FLOW-02 (dropped body) and FLOW-08 (switch expressions).

title: Catch bodies collapse into one opaque statement because the catch parameter is dropped
evidence: The Java adapter does not map catch_formal_parameter, so the reducer drops it. In build_try the first child of NN_CATCH_CLAUSE is then the body block: it goes in as a single statement through add_stmt_to_current, next_sibling() is None, and the body is never dispatched. resolve_catch_type always sees a block and returns u32::MAX.
impact: Even after FLOW-01 is fixed, returns, throws and branches inside catch blocks produce no edges, and the catch variable is never defined.
recommendation: Keep catch_formal_parameter as NN_PARAM_DECL, or find the body by node type instead of position. Dispatch the block and define the catch variable. This differs from FLOW-07 (exception-edge semantics).

title: CGCSR::edges_of panics on the caller CSR
evidence: edges_of checks `end <= adj.len()` but then slices `edge_types[start..end]`. caller_csr is built and deserialized with `edge_types: Vec::new()`, so edges_of panics with an out-of-range slice for any method whose CSR offset is non-zero. Nothing calls it yet, but it is public API.
impact: The first who-calls-me query through this public accessor crashes the process.
recommendation: Also check edge_types.len() and return an empty kind slice, or store caller edge kinds; separate types for the two CSRs would be cleaner. Add a unit test that calls caller_csr.edges_of.

title: Hot-loop trace logging is always formatted and flushed to two log files
evidence: Phases 4-6 emit one format!-built log line per call site and about eight per function. log_event writes every level to both the persistent and session files under a mutex, with two write_all and two flush calls, whatever the console level. The CLI enables both files (main.rs:129).
impact: Millions of flushed writes and unbounded log growth on large codebases.
recommendation: Gate formatting behind a level check or a macro, filter file output by level, keep per-site and per-function messages at trace, and stop flushing on every line.

title: Lambda parameters never become SK_PARAM symbols
evidence: Only formal_parameter and spread_parameter map to NN_PARAM_DECL. A lambda's single identifier parameter becomes NN_IDENTIFIER_EXPR, and inferred_parameters (`(a, b) ->`) hits `_ => Drop`. So `x -> ...` and `(a, b) -> ...` create no SK_PARAM, count_params gives the lambda 0, and the lambda is named after its parameter. Lambda parameters are not in SYM-12's list.
impact: Most lambda parameters are invisible to scopes, SSA def-use and metrics.
recommendation: Emit NN_PARAM_DECL for a lambda's identifier parameter and for each identifier in inferred_parameters, set param_count, and give lambdas a synthetic name. Test both lambda forms.

title: Scope-graph serialization is lossy and its fields mislead consumers
evidence: Only ScopeRecords are written. Per-scope declaration lists, import edges and import mappings are not, import_table_off is always 0, and first_decl/decl_count imply a contiguous id range even though declarations are interleaved. ScopeKind has no Package kind, and at HEAD resolve_sym_package treats scope_kind 1 (Class) as a package scope. This differs from SYM-14, which covers the dropped type_ref_resolutions.
impact: Consumers cannot redo or audit resolution from .sta, and scope-based package lookup misreads the records.
recommendation: Serialize declaration lists in CSR form (offsets plus symbol ids) and import tables with real offsets. Redefine or remove first_decl. Add a Package scope kind or document that packages are not scopes. Add a round-trip test for scope membership.

title: Anonymous class bodies and instance initializers get no declaration node
evidence: object_creation_expression is Keep(NN_NEW_EXPR) but its class_body is Eliminate (java.rs:110), so anonymous-class methods become direct children of NN_NEW_EXPR. An instance initializer (a bare block in class_body) is emitted as a plain NN_BLOCK, and NN_JAVA_INSTANCE_INIT is never produced. grep shows SK_ANON_CLASS and SK_INSTANCE_INIT are never created.
impact: Anonymous-class methods are parented to the enclosing method, which breaks dispatch and UML. Initializer code is not analyzed as a body.
recommendation: Emit an NN_CLASS_DECL with an anonymous flag in NodeAttr for a class_body under object_creation_expression or enum_constant, and map bare class-body blocks to NN_JAVA_INSTANCE_INIT.

title: A reloaded .tca cannot name its files: read() discards the paths and path_str_offset is reinterpreted
evidence: TokenCorpusArtifact has no path field. read() skips the path section (247-251) and returns the on-disk byte offset in path_str_offset. server.rs:714 and class_diagram.rs:132 resolve that field with interner.lookup_text as a text_id, its in-memory meaning (mod.rs:138), so after read() only file 0 resolves correctly. This differs from CORE-07: it is consumer-side data loss.
impact: Any tool built on TokenCorpusSerializer::read reports wrong file names in traces and in test-file detection.
recommendation: Add a file_paths field filled by both run() and read(), and give path_str_offset one documented meaning. Have write() take paths from the artifact; today a longer file_paths slice panics at serializer.rs:97. Add a round-trip test on resolved paths.

title: The tca_hash link and Phase 2 invariants 2-5 are documented as enforced but never checked
evidence: The spec says finalize() enforces Invariants 1-5 and that Phase 3 rejects a mismatched (TCA, BPA) pair. finalize() asserts only Invariant 1. No code compares bpa.tca_hash with the CRC of the .tca: symbol/serializer.rs:42-43 recomputes the CRCs but only stores them. The 'hash' is also a CRC-64, which is not collision-resistant.
impact: A stale or foreign .bpa paired with a different .tca is accepted silently, giving misattributed tokens and symbols.
recommendation: Verify bpa.tca_hash in Phase 3 and in the server, and fail with a clear error. Check Invariants 2-4 in debug builds or tests, consider SHA-256 for provenance links, and correct the spec.

title: Phase 2 silently skips files it cannot open or parse, and reopens paths relative to the working directory
evidence: Phase 2 rebuilds paths from the .tca, where they were stored with to_string_lossy exactly as given (often relative), and calls fs::read from the current directory. A non-UTF-8 path, a moved file, a different CWD or a parse failure each falls through nested `if let` with no else branch and no warning (mod.rs:141-154). This differs from CORE-10, which covers repeated reads.
impact: A file can have tokens but no AST and no error. Downstream phases quietly miss its classes and methods.
recommendation: Store canonical absolute paths, or a source root plus relative paths. Carry the bytes or a content hash over from Phase 1. Return an error, or at least log_warn with counts, for every skipped file.

title: SCPGPipelineBuilder::execute returns Result, but phases 7 to 10 panic on I/O errors
evidence: Phase7Stage::run through Phase10Stage::run return their artifacts directly and call panic! or expect when writing .tra, .psa, .uma or .scpg fails. execute() calls them without catch_unwind, so a full disk or a read-only output directory aborts the caller instead of yielding Err.
impact: Library and server callers crash on ordinary write failures. The builder's error contract is false.
recommendation: Change the four run() signatures to return Result, propagate with `?` in execute(), main.rs and server.rs, and add a test that uses a read-only output directory.

title: CGCSR::edges_of panics on the caller CSR because its edge_types array is always empty
evidence: edges_of checks `end <= self.adj.len()` and then slices `&self.edge_types[start..end]`. The caller CSR is built with `edge_types: Vec::new()` both in cg/mod.rs:175 and in the deserializer (serializer.rs:213). For any method with a caller, the slice range exceeds length 0 and panics. Nothing calls it yet, so the bug is latent.
impact: The first code that queries callers through this public API will crash on any non-leaf method.
recommendation: Bound the slice by edge_types.len() or fill the caller edge types. Better, give CGCSR a constructor that enforces equal adj and edge_types lengths. Add a unit test that calls caller_csr.edges_of.

title: The generic reducer erases identifiers and mis-types nodes by substring matching, even for JavaScript
evidence: identifier, property_identifier and JS formal_parameters fall to `_ => Eliminate`, so names and parameters produce no nodes. Kinds containing 'expression' become NN_EXPR_STMT (e.g. augmented_assignment_expression), and kinds containing 'declaration' become NN_LOCAL_VAR_DECL (e.g. generator_function_declaration). function and arrow_function map to NN_METHOD_DECL, super maps to NN_THIS_EXPR, and encode_attrs always returns 0. This differs from CORE-01, which is about wrong grammars.
impact: JS ASTs carry no names, parameters or operators. Closures become methods and compound assignments are not treated as definitions.
recommendation: Replace the substring heuristics with explicit per-grammar tables. Keep identifiers as NN_IDENTIFIER_EXPR, map function expressions to NN_LAMBDA_EXPR and augmented assignments to NN_ASSIGN_EXPR, and encode operators.

title: type_parameters becomes one NN_TYPE_PARAM node and each type_parameter is dropped
evidence: java.rs:83 keeps 'type_parameters', the whole `<K, V extends X>` list, as NN_TYPE_PARAM, while 'type_parameter' has no arm and is dropped. Because every child vanishes, the node's token range is just the `<` token. The semantic adapter turns that node into a single SK_TYPE_PARAM.
impact: Generic classes and methods get one nameless type-parameter symbol instead of one per parameter, and their bounds are lost.
recommendation: Eliminate type_parameters and Keep each type_parameter as NN_TYPE_PARAM, with its type_identifier and type_bound children.

title: select1 scans bit by bit and is O(n) for absent ranks; every navigation call pays this despite the O(1) claims
evidence: select1 binary-searches the superblocks, then loops over positions to bit_count calling bounds-checked get_bit for each bit (512 or more iterations), and scans to the end when the rank is missing. rank1 also builds its partial byte one bit at a time. first_child, next_sibling, subtree_size, is_leaf, depth and lca all start with a select1 call. This differs from CORE-06, which covers correctness.
impact: CFG and symbol traversals do hundreds of bit probes per step, far from the documented O(1) navigation.
recommendation: Store an open_pos[preorder] array or a sampled select index, use word popcount and broadword select, and correct the complexity claims in the docs.

title: Console logging uses println!/eprintln!, which panic on a closed pipe, and it mixes logs into stdout
evidence: log_event writes Info, Warn, Debug and Trace with println! and only Error with eprintln!. Both macros panic when the write fails, for example `openheart analyze src | head` (broken pipe) or a server whose console has closed. Warnings land on stdout alongside any program output. This differs from CORE-13, which covers the file sinks and the mutex.
impact: The CLI, or a server thread, can panic mid-run because a terminal or pipe closed.
recommendation: Write with writeln! to a locked stderr and ignore write errors, send all diagnostics to stderr, and keep stdout for command output.

title: Unseeded FNV-1a with low-bit indexing makes string interning hash-floodable
evidence: ADR-001 (technical-decisions.md:9-13) picks FNV-1a over SipHash and lists 'avalanche-free distribution' as a benefit. interner.rs:53 uses slot = hash & mask with linear probing (70). FNV-1a's low k bits depend only on the low k bits of state and input, so low-bit multicollisions can be chained cheaply. The server analyses arbitrary repos (AUTO-02).
impact: A crafted repository can make interning quadratic, a CPU denial of service against the server.
recommendation: Use a randomly keyed hash (SipHash-1-3, ahash or foldhash) for the table, and keep FNV only where a stable persisted hash is needed. Correct the ADR rationale and add a collision stress test.

title: The paper's Limitations section cites mitigations the code does not implement
evidence: tex:1311-1314 claims non-series-parallel CFGs get k<=3 unwinding via Valdes SP recognition. No SP recognizer exists, and RecursiveHandler::apply returns f_paths unchanged (recursive.rs:26-28), for recursion only. tex:1320-1324 says reflective sites are tagged CG_Reflection, but CG_EDGE_REFLECTION (cg.rs:13) is unused. tex:1391 calls a full implementation 'future work'. 'Anderson' (785, 1317) should be Andersen.
impact: The stated soundness boundaries are fictional, which overstates where the theorems apply.
recommendation: Implement SP detection and reflection tagging, or rewrite Limitations to match the code. Reconcile the paper's status with the README and fix the author name.

title: Phase10Stage::run panics on I/O failure instead of returning Result
evidence: src/scpg/mod.rs:53-55 wraps SCPGSerializer::write in .expect("Phase 10: Failed to write unified .scpg binary file"). Its callers return Result and use ?/map_err for every other phase: SCPGPipelineBuilder::execute (src/core/pipeline.rs:151, 223) and cmd_analyze (src/main.rs:101, 243). The spec declares -> Result<OpenHeartEngine> (docs/plans/phase10.md:302). The written file is never re-opened to validate it.
impact: A read-only output dir, full disk or locked file aborts the CLI or a library caller instead of returning an error.
recommendation: Return io::Result<OpenHeartEngine> (or a typed error) and propagate it with ? in pipeline.rs and main.rs. Optionally re-open the file with OpenHeartEngine::open to validate it, and pass a PipelineArtifacts-style struct instead of 10 positional parameters.

title: scpg_hash changes on every run, so it is not a content fingerprint
evidence: bpa.tca_hash is crc64 of the whole .tca file (src/ast/mod.rs:48). The .tca header embeds SystemTime::now() (src/ingestion/serializer.rs:80-84), file mtimes (:115) and paths as given (:93-101). That hash, the link hashes derived from it, and tra.hashes.tca_hash (crc of Debug(file_records), which includes mtime_ns, hash_chain.rs:36) all feed compose_scpg_hash (serializer/mod.rs:124-134).
impact: Identical sources get a new scpg_hash on every run, so cross-run caching, staleness checks and 'hash unchanged' incremental semantics cannot work.
recommendation: Hash content only: keep timestamps, mtimes and absolute paths out of link hashes (for example, use sorted content_sha256 plus relative paths), or give each artifact a deterministic content hash. Add a test that builds the same sources twice and asserts equal scpg_hash. This is distinct from SCPG-13's header timestamp field.

title: Header source_hash is always zero, so a stale .scpg cannot be detected
evidence: src/scpg/serializer/mod.rs:146 writes [0u8; 32] as source_hash. The spec defines it as SHA-256 of sorted per-file SHA-256s (docs/plans/phase10.md:24) and claims it 'detects out-of-date SCPG' (:549). Ingestion already computes per-file content_sha256 (src/ingestion/mod.rs:55-58) and a source_tree_hash (:93-97) that it writes into the .tca. Nothing reads the field.
impact: Consumers cannot tell whether a .scpg matches the current sources, so they may serve a stale graph.
recommendation: Compute SHA-256 over the sorted (relative path, content_sha256) pairs from tca.file_records, write it at offset 16, and add an is_up_to_date(sources) check that OpenHeartEngine::open and the CLI can use.

title: The test-source filter only matches absolute forward-slash paths, so Windows and relative runs include test classes
evidence: Paths are interned with to_string_lossy(), which keeps native separators. The filter only checks contains('/src/test/'), '/src/tests/' and '/__tests__/'. So D:\proj\src\test\FooTest.java on Windows and relative 'src/test/...' paths never match. This differs from UML-05, which is about filters dropping real user types.
impact: The same sources give different class diagrams on Windows and Linux, and for relative and absolute inputs.
recommendation: Normalize separators, match path components (test, tests, androidTest, __tests__), and make the rule configurable. Add test_windows_and_relative_test_paths_filtered.

title: Phase9Stage::run panics when the .uma write fails and cannot return an error
evidence: run() returns a bare UMLMetadataArtifact and calls panic! when UMASerializer::write fails (disk full, permissions, missing directory). SCPGPipelineBuilder::execute returns a Result but cannot pass this error on, and the server process dies. Phases 3 to 6 return Result.
impact: An ordinary I/O error crashes the CLI or server instead of being reported.
recommendation: Return Result<UMLMetadataArtifact, io::Error> and map the error at each call site. Add a test that writes to an unwritable path and expects Err.

title: Server collects ~60 extensions the pipeline cannot parse
evidence: collect_files accepts py, rs, go, c/cpp, sh, sql, rb, php, asm and more (server.rs:807-867). AdapterRegistry registers only Java, Kotlin (parsed with the Java grammar) and JavaScript, and sends every other language to a JavaScript-grammar fallback (registry.rs:24-57, kotlin.rs:29-30). The suite's own target, the OpenHeart repo (scripts/test_full_suite.py:129), is mostly Rust, Python and JS.
impact: Shell, SQL, C and Python files are tokenized as JavaScript, which pollutes results and wastes time on polyglot repos.
recommendation: Collect only extensions that have a registered adapter (query AdapterRegistry), make the set configurable, and report skipped-file counts in stats. Test: a repo with Foo.java and build.sh yields only Foo.

title: Hand-built JSON responses are invalid for common error strings
evidence: Phase 1-6 error branches insert the raw error string (server.rs:530-604), and ingestion errors contain Debug-quoted paths (src/ingestion/mod.rs:52). The no-sources branch embeds target_dir.display() (server.rs:495-502), which on Windows contains sequences like ./target_repos\FractalAndroid. escape_json_str leaves other control characters unescaped (server.rs:701-707). Node's JSON.parse rejects all three cases.
impact: Clients get a parse error instead of the failure reason; on Windows every missing-sources error is unparseable.
recommendation: Build every response with serde_json (json! or Serialize structs), including error paths, and delete escape_json_str. Test: each error branch's body parses with serde_json::from_str.

title: On Windows the temp dir is not deleted while corpus.tca is still mapped
evidence: stage_input owns a MemoryMappedFile of corpus.tca (server.rs:539-546) and lives until process_analyze_request returns, but remove_dir_all runs earlier (server.rs:693). Windows refuses to delete a file with a live mapped view, and let _ = hides the failure.
impact: Under run.bat, even successful analyses leave their artifacts in %TEMP%.
recommendation: Drop stage_input before cleanup (put the pipeline in its own block) and log cleanup errors. Add a Windows CI test that the session dir is gone after a request.

title: /api/supported-languages advertises languages that are not supported
evidence: server.rs:82-85 lists java, python, typescript, javascript, cpp, rust and go, and omits kotlin. Only Java, Kotlin (via the Java grammar) and JavaScript adapters exist (registry.rs:24-39, kotlin.rs:29-30); every other language falls back to the JavaScript grammar.
impact: Clients are told Python, Rust, Go and C++ work, and get JavaScript-grammar garbage instead.
recommendation: Generate the list from AdapterRegistry with an accuracy or maturity flag per language, and include Kotlin with its caveat.

title: Security doc presents CRC-64 and SHA-256 as tamper protection
evidence: docs/security-architecture.md:16-20 titles the section 'Tamper Protection', but CRC-64 is unkeyed and anyone can recompute it. The stored SHA-256 digests are written (serializer.rs:77, 109) but never re-verified. Ingestion also hashes one read of each file and tokenizes a second read (mod.rs:53, 111). Differs from SRV-14.
impact: Users may treat artifacts as tamper-evident when they only detect accidental corruption.
recommendation: Reword the section as corruption detection, or add an HMAC or signature and verify source hashes on load. Hash and tokenize the same buffer.

title: Logger writes every level, including trace, to two unbuffered files from hot loops
evidence: core/logger.rs:124-159 gates only the console output by level (136). Every call still takes a global Mutex (145), formats a timestamped line (147), and write_all+flushes it to two unbuffered File handles (149-157); callers' format! arguments are built eagerly. Hot callers: a trace per call site (cg/call_sites.rs:57); per-function trace and debug lines (cfg/mod.rs:78,86; ssa/mod.rs:47,83,114; placement, renaming, liveness, cdg, ifds); INFO per function in Phase 8 (psa/mod.rs:131); INFO per class (pass1_discovery.rs:151; class_diagram.rs:56). The persistent log is append-only and never rotated.
impact: At 1M LOC this produces millions of lines, roughly 0.5–1 GB of logs and tens of seconds of syscalls per run, heavy console output on Windows, and a persistent log that grows without bound.
recommendation: Use tracing with EnvFilter, whose macros check the level before formatting, and tracing-appender non_blocking with rolling, size-capped files. Downgrade per-element INFO and DIAG lines to trace, or aggregate them into per-phase counters. Open the session and persistent logs only when requested.

title: Bitwise CRC-64 recomputed 19 times over re-read artifacts, whole-file buffers, and duplicate token tables
evidence: ingestion/serializer.rs:16-29 computes CRC-64 bit by bit (8 iterations per byte), and integrity.rs and hash_chain.rs compute CRC-32 the same way. main.rs re-reads .tca, .bpa, .cfa, .ssa and .tra (154, 163, 180, 192, 226) only so later phases can re-hash them: TCA, BPA, STA and CFA are hashed three times each (ast/mod.rs:48; symbol/serializer.rs:42-43; cfg/mod.rs:30-31; ssa/mod.rs:41; cg/mod.rs:45-46; psa/mod.rs:77). Serializers build the whole file in a Vec first, and SymbolTableArtifact::build clones every builder table (symbol/serializer.rs:64-71). TCA stores token_records and token_entries as identical copies (builder.rs:30-31).
impact: At 1M LOC this means gigabytes of bitwise CRC (seconds to tens of seconds) plus redundant I/O, a 2× memory spike per phase, and a TCA of 32 B/token instead of 16.
recommendation: Hash once while streaming through a BufWriter with an incremental hasher, and pass the digest forward in memory. Use a SIMD CRC (crc64fast-nvme or crc-fast), or xxh3 (xxhash-rust) for integrity and BLAKE3 for content addressing. Move builder tables instead of cloning them. Drop the duplicate backward table, since token_id order already equals sort order.

title: Remaining quadratic helpers: per-function CSR builds, adjacency dedup, per-class TH scans, O(depth) node closes
evidence: cfg/builder/mod.rs:150-151 and 165-166 build the successor and predecessor CSRs by scanning all edges for every block, O(B·E) per function. cg/mod.rs:118-124 deduplicates adjacency with .any/.contains, O(Σdeg²), and sizes the CSR and Tarjan by all symbols (110). class_diagram.rs:283 and the pattern detectors (query.rs:42, strategy.rs:15, composite.rs:16, decorator.rs:15) scan all th_edges for each class. loops.rs:63-81 allocates and sweeps n entries per back edge. frontier.rs:25 and cdg.rs:77 deduplicate with Vec::contains. ast/builder.rs:166 walks the open stack on every close.
impact: Each is tolerable on small inputs but superlinear on giant generated methods, hub methods and 10^5-edge hierarchies, costing seconds to minutes each at 1M LOC.
recommendation: Build CSRs by counting sort (degree count, prefix sum, fill) in O(B+E). Deduplicate with sort+dedup or a HashSet, and size arrays by method count. Build one TH out-edge CSR shared by all extractors. Mark loop bodies with bitsets in a single pass, use bitsets for DF/CDG membership, and delete close_node's ancestor loop, since the reducer already returns merged ranges.

title: Phase 2 re-reads and re-parses every file and re-derives token ids by position; the two token-id spaces match only by accident
evidence: Phase 2 ignores the in-memory TokenCorpusArtifact, then re-reads each path stored in the .tca and re-parses it (ast/mod.rs:136-155).
