Phase 1 had already read every file twice (ingestion/mod.rs:53,111), and its SHA-256 is never re-checked. Nodes are matched to tokens by (file, line, col), falling back to any token on the same line, possibly one before the node (reducer.rs:95-117). Columns wrap in Phase 1 (`as u16`, walker.rs:59) but saturate in Phase 2 (reducer.rs:56). Phase 1 ids follow allocation order (first_token_id, token_entries), while Phases 2-10 index the sorted token_records. path_str_offset is an interner id in memory (ingestion/mod.rs:138) but a byte offset on disk (ingestion/serializer.rs:93-101).
impact: Front-end cost roughly doubles. A file edited mid-run, or a line longer than 65,535 columns, silently misaligns AST token ranges, so names, spans and links attach to the wrong tokens. A reloaded .tca resolves the wrong paths.
recommendation: Parse once: build the BP AST in the same CST walk that emits tokens, recording each leaf's token index directly, or keep each tree_sitter::Tree in memory between phases. If any phase re-reads a file, verify its SHA-256 first. Keep a single TokenIdx space (the sorted index) and assert in finalize that allocation order matches it. Give path_str_offset the same meaning in memory and on disk.

title: Phase 3 drops its resolution indices at the boundary, so later phases rescan symbols linearly without name resolution
evidence: SymbolTableBuilder holds node_to_symbol, type_ref_resolutions and per-scope import maps (symbol/builder.rs:24-30; scope_graph/mod.rs:15-16). SymbolTableArtifact carries none of them (symbol/serializer.rs:13-34,41-75), and scopes are written with import_table_off = 0 and no import table (symbol/serializer.rs:124-136). The Java reducer drops import_declaration and package_declaration (`_ => Drop`, ast/adapter/java.rs:129). Pass 2 therefore never sees a Java import (pass2_imports.rs:20-28), and Pass 1 rescans raw tokens for `package` (pass1_discovery.rs:464-575). All files share one import scope (pass2_imports.rs:15-18). Phase 6 rescans every symbol for each ancestor of each call (call_sites.rs:70-91; resolution.rs:185-235).
impact: Later phases cannot resolve receiver types or imported names, which is a root cause of E2E-01 and E2E-04. Call extraction costs O(calls x depth x symbols) on large repositories.
recommendation: Export from Phase 3, as CSR arrays in .sta, the maps node->symbol and reference site->resolved symbol and type, plus per-file import tables. Model them on CodeQL's binding relations or Kythe ref edges keyed by VNames. Keep import and package declarations as NN_IMPORT and NN_PACKAGE nodes in Phase 2, give every file its own scope, and have Phase 6 resolve calls through these tables in O(1) per site.

title: Cross-phase id fields are narrowed to u8/u16 without checks, and exporters silently keep only the first 3-12 items, with different caps per format
evidence: file_id is u16 (core/types/source.rs:11; token.rs:121-124), so with more than 65,536 files sort keys collide and Phase 1 aborts (ingestion/builder.rs:49-56). SSARecord.def_block is truncated to u8 (core/types/ssa.rs:43) yet read as a block id by TRA and PSA (ssa_bi.rs:20,35; feasibility.rs:115-119). The phi orig_sym_id is written as u16 (ssa/serializer.rs:113), SymbolSpanRecord lines are u16 (tra/types.rs:76-84; sym_span.rs:38-40), and tokens and strings are capped at 65,535 bytes (walker.rs:54; interner.rs:99-101). Exporters keep only the first N items, and N differs by format: activity take(6) in PlantUML vs take(8) in Mermaid, and CFG take(4) vs take(3) (plantuml.rs:958,1262; mermaid.rs:1131,1397).
impact: Methods over 256 blocks, files over 65,535 lines and repositories over 65,536 files produce wrong spans, wrong block attribution or aborts. Diagrams of large projects omit most content, and what they omit differs by format.
recommendation: Use u32 for every cross-phase id and convert with checked try_from, recording a diagnostic on overflow. Replace silent take(N) with configurable limits applied identically in every format, and record 'shown/total' in diagram metadata. Add proptest-generated large inputs to CI: a 300-block method, a 70k-line file and a synthetic 70k-file tree.

title: Artifact readers trust header counts and offsets, and inspect reports integrity it never checks
evidence: The readers check a CRC-64, which any attacker can recompute. After that they index `buf[offset..offset+4]` without checking how many bytes remain: TRA (tra/serializer.rs:174-280), PSA (psa/serializer.rs:201-245, including `pos = metrics_offset` taken from the file), UMA (uma/serializer.rs:272 onward) and BPA (ast/serializer.rs:118-171). Short files therefore panic. Counts from u32 headers go straight into Vec::with_capacity (symbol/serializer.rs:240, cg/serializer.rs:158, ingestion/serializer.rs:254,296), so large counts abort on a multi-GiB allocation. scpg/mmap/mod.rs:52-62 reads section_count entries unchecked, and get_section computes `start + byte_length` (86-90), which can wrap. inspect prints 'CRC-64 Check : VERIFIED VALID' for .tca and .bpa files without checking anything (main.rs:373-389).
impact: `openheart inspect`, the documented validation tool, panics or aborts on small crafted files and claims integrity it never verified. Library users who load artifacts inherit the same crashes.
recommendation: Parse through one bounds-checked cursor: a Reader that returns Err on short reads, or zerocopy, binrw or scroll. Check `count <= remaining / record_size` before allocating, and use try_reserve and checked_add for offsets. Make inspect verify the CRC for every artifact type and report the real error. Add cargo-fuzz targets for each format, seeded with real artifacts. Done when 24 hours of libFuzzer finds no crash.

title: No work or memory budgets, and several phases scale super-linearly on realistic large inputs
evidence: Nothing bounds per-function or per-run work. Switch constraints perform k(k-1)/2 BDD applies (constraints.rs:122-127), each of which clears the apply cache (bdd/mod.rs:78). edge_index_of is a linear scan on every lookup (rpo.rs:106-108). The CFG CSR build is O(blocks x edges) (cfg/builder/mod.rs:150-172). close_node walks every ancestor (ast/builder.rs:163-175). CHA rescans every symbol per call site (cg/resolution.rs:84). The RMQ stores n(log n+1) u32 values (rmq.rs:28-48), about 0.9 GB for 10M BP bits. Each source is read three times and parsed twice, with no size cap or tree-sitter timeout (ingestion/mod.rs:53,111; tree_sitter.rs:17-24). OPENHEART_MAX_MEMORY_MB in .env.example is never read.
impact: Giant switches in JavaCC- or ANTLR-generated code, deep nesting and 1M-LOC repositories make phases quadratic or memory-bound. That is a DoS on the server and contradicts the 128x compression claim.
recommendation: Index edges with a HashMap<(u32,u32),usize> or CSR offsets, and build the CSR by counting sort. Encode exactly-one constraints with a linear sequential counter, and keep a persistent computed table with a per-function node budget (CUDD style). Precompute subtype closures for CHA. Replace the sparse table with a range min-max tree (Navarro-Sadakane) or a block-decomposed RMQ using O(n) bits. Parse each file once, and implement the documented memory limits plus Parser::set_timeout_micros.

title: Phase 2 re-reads sources by a lossy path and silently drops files it cannot re-read or re-parse
evidence: Phase 2 does not reuse Phase 1's bytes or parse trees. It decodes paths from the .tca (ast/mod.rs:85-99), then re-reads and re-parses each file inside nested `if let Ok` blocks that have no else branch and no log (141-153). Phase 1 stored the paths with to_string_lossy (ingestion/serializer.rs:94, ingestion/mod.rs:137), so a Latin-1 file name becomes U+FFFD and the re-read fails silently. A file edited between phases is parsed from different bytes than it was tokenized from, and tok_table_lookup (reducer.rs:95-117) then binds nodes to the nearest token on the same line. Phase 1 itself hashes one read (mod.rs:53) and tokenizes a second one (mod.rs:111).
impact: Files silently disappear from the AST, CFG and UML output while their tokens remain, and token ranges can point at the wrong tokens. Nothing tells the user or a benchmark harness.
recommendation: Read each file once into an immutable snapshot (bytes plus content hash) shared by all phases, and reuse the Phase 1 tree or store byte offsets in the .tca. Carry paths as OsString or raw bytes (OsStrExt, os_str_bytes) instead of lossy strings. Emit a per-file diagnostics list in every artifact and API response.

title: Error model is panic or abort-the-run: I/O panics, release-mode asserts, and per-unit failures that fail everything
evidence: Phases 7-10 return artifacts rather than Result, and they panic on I/O failure (tra/mod.rs:42-43, psa/mod.rs:153-154, uma/mod.rs:97-98, and an expect at scpg/mod.rs:53-55). Invariants are enforced with release-mode assert!/assert_eq! (tra/builder.rs:66-131, ast/builder.rs:180-207, jump_table.rs:23-29). In the other direction, one function that fails a CFG or SSA invariant aborts the whole run through `?` (cfg/mod.rs:84, ssa/mod.rs:81), and so does one unreadable file (ingestion/mod.rs:51-54). Locks are taken with lock().unwrap() (logger.rs:82,145; ingestion/mod.rs:136,174).
impact: A full disk or a read-only output directory crashes the CLI with a backtrace and kills the server. One unusual function or file throws away the results for the entire repository.
recommendation: Thread one thiserror enum (already a dependency) through every Phase*Stage::run. Turn per-function and per-file invariant failures into a diagnostic plus a skipped unit, optionally wrapped in catch_unwind per unit, and keep the partial artifacts. Reserve assert! for genuinely impossible states. Enforce clippy deny(unwrap_used, expect_used, panic, indexing_slicing) on non-test code in CI.

title: Ten-phase orchestration is hand-wired at 18 call sites through positional raw-hash parameters, and has already broken the hash chain
evidence: The ten-phase wiring is hand-copied at 18 IngestionStage::run call sites: main.rs:150-255, core/pipeline.rs:170-225, adapters/server.rs:527-615 and 13 test files. PipelineStageTemplate (pipeline.rs:34-78) has no implementors. SCPGPipelineBuilder never reads its diagram_formats field and defaults to the shared temp directory with fixed file names (pipeline.rs:113,159-168). Stages take long positional argument lists with adjacent raw `&[u8]` hash inputs (cg/mod.rs:37-38; Phase 9 takes 10 arguments). That plumbing has already broken the chain: psa/mod.rs:78 stores `cfa.sta_hash` in the PSA's 'CRC-64 of the SSA artifact' field (psa/serializer.rs:37).
impact: Every fix must be repeated at 18 sites, and the copies drift: the server ignores errors the CLI reports. Swapped hashes compile without complaint, and concurrent runs with default settings overwrite each other's artifacts.
recommendation: Make one orchestrator the only entry point for the CLI, the server and tests: a typed stage DAG in which each artifact is a newtype carrying its own content digest (for example Artifact<Tca> with .digest()), so hashes cannot be swapped. Default to a per-run tempfile::TempDir. For incremental runs, use Salsa queries (as rust-analyzer and Astral's ty do) instead of re-running every phase. Provide a test helper such as analyze_fixture(src) returning PipelineArtifacts.

title: The single-threaded pipeline reads every file three times, parses each twice, and logs through a logger that formats and flushes on every event
evidence: There is no rayon or threading anywhere, though .env.example:14 advertises OPENHEART_NUM_THREADS, which the code never reads. Each file is read three times (ingestion/mod.rs:53,111; ast/mod.rs:142) and parsed twice (ingestion/mod.rs:117; ast/mod.rs:143). The SHA-256 recorded on the first read is never checked against the later reads. Log call sites run format! before the level check. Every event, whatever its level, is written to two files and flushed under a global Mutex (logger.rs:124-159). Phase 8 logs one INFO line per function (psa/mod.rs:132), and a debug println! remains in library code (generic.rs:27). The external-type lookup scans every symbol for each reference (pass3_types.rs:108-116).
impact: Throughput is single-core and I/O-bound, and the symbol fallback costs O(types x symbols), so large repositories will be slow or appear to hang. A file edited during a run gets tokens that no longer match its recorded SHA.
recommendation: Read each file once into an Arc<[u8]>, parse it once, and hand the tree or reduced CST to Phase 2. Parallelize per file in Phases 1-2 and per function in Phases 4, 5 and 8 with rayon, merging results deterministically. Replace the logger with tracing and tracing-subscriber: EnvFilter on RUST_LOG, per-phase spans, and a buffered non-blocking file writer from tracing-appender. Index external symbols in a HashMap, and confirm the gains with the ENG-08 harness.

title: No polyglot model: Java-Kotlin interop and language boundaries are not represented
evidence: Android and other JVM repos mix Java and Kotlin in one module, yet SymbolRecord has no language, binary name or JVM descriptor (src/core/types/symbol.rs:96-117). Kotlin file facades (FooKt), @JvmName/@JvmStatic, and the mapping from properties to getters (`user.getName()` calls Kotlin `name`) are not modelled. Call targets are matched by token position (src/cg/resolution.rs:178-239). Java `native` is never recorded (src/ast/adapter/java.rs:149-157 sets only static, final and abstract), so the JNI boundary stubs the paper promises (docs/openheart_research_paper.tex:1326-1330) cannot exist.
impact: In mixed JVM projects, the most common real polyglot case, cross-language calls and type uses are lost or bound only through coincidental simple names.
recommendation: Model the JVM languages in one namespace keyed by binary names and descriptors, as CodeQL does (its Kotlin extractor writes into the Java database schema) and Joern does (kotlin2cpg emits the same CPG as javasrc2cpg). Synthesize Kotlin facade classes and accessor aliases. Add explicit boundary nodes for JNI native, Kotlin external, FFI/ctypes and gRPC/OpenAPI stubs. Done = a mixed Java/Kotlin fixture with call and type edges in both directions.

title: No heap or field SSA (Memory SSA)
evidence: Only local identifiers are versioned. Field and array accesses have no memory versions, SSA_FLAG_IS_FIELD_DEF is never set, and calls carry no may-def or may-use of heap state.
impact: Flow through fields, arrays and object state, which is most Java data flow, is invisible to SSA, IFDS and slicing.
recommendation: Add Memory SSA (heap φs per alias class from points-to), or field-based SSA for this.f accesses, plus may-def/may-use summaries at call sites.

title: There is no Kotlin semantic adapter or Kotlin standard-library model
evidence: Phase3Stage::run always builds JavaSemanticAdapter, whatever each file's language. Kotlin files therefore get Java primitives (Int, Long, Unit and Any are not recognized), Java stubs only (no kotlin.collections List or MutableList), and Java default visibility, although Kotlin defaults to public. SymbolKind has no kinds for object, companion, typealias or property.
impact: Most Kotlin type references become SK_EXTERNAL, and Kotlin visibility and declaration kinds are wrong.
recommendation: Pick a SemanticAdapter per file from its LangId. Add a Kotlin adapter with Kotlin primitives, public by default, implicit kotlin.* imports and built-in type stubs, plus symbol kinds for object, companion and typealias.

title: The documented annotation table and UML metadata section do not exist, and annotations are never recorded
evidence: phase3.md lists a UML METADATA section and a per-symbol ANNOTATION TABLE in .sta, with uml_meta_offset pointing into it. The serializer writes neither, and uml_meta_offset is always 0. No pass records which annotations (@Override, @Entity, @Autowired, @Nonnull) a declaration carries, which is why Pass 1 relies on hardcoded annotation-name lists.
impact: Framework-aware analysis (Spring/JPA stereotypes, @Override checks, nullability for composition) has no data to work from.
recommendation: Resolve the NN_ANNOTATION_USE children of declarations in Pass 3 and store (symbol, annotation type, argument summary) records with an offset index. Serialize them, and either populate uml_meta_offset or remove it from the spec.

title: Phases 1 and 2 have no incremental path, although hashes are recorded and the docs promise one
evidence: Per-file SHA-256 hashes and mtimes are stored but never compared. parse(source, None) never reuses an old tree or applies an InputEdit. Token ids and preorder indices form one global space with no per-file segments, so any edit renumbers everything. The docs describe incremental CST parsing and BP excision and insertion.
impact: Every change re-ingests and re-encodes the whole project, so IDE-style synchronization is impossible.
recommendation: Segment the corpus and the BP per file (file-local ids plus offset tables), skip files whose SHA-256 is unchanged, and keep per-file trees so tree-sitter can reparse incrementally.

title: No incremental recomputation: ids are positions in the whole corpus and the incremental engine is a stub
evidence: IncrementalEngine::apply_delta rebuilds nothing and returns `current_hash ^ 0x0101_0101` (scpg/incremental/mod.rs:26-34). RebuildPlanner relies on booleans supplied by the caller, and StaleDetector is never called (tra/delta/invalidation.rs:10-12). Every id is a position in the whole corpus: token indices are global sort positions, AST ids are preorder positions in one forest, and symbol ids follow discovery order (symbol/builder.rs:68). Editing file k therefore renumbers every id after it. Per-file SHA-256 is computed (ingestion/mod.rs:56-59) but never used as a cache key.
impact: Every edit forces a full 10-phase rebuild, which rules out IDE and incremental-CI use, and no result can be reused or diffed across versions.
recommendation: Make the file the unit. Ids become (FileId, local), with FileId interned from the root-relative path, and Phases 1-3 are cached per file, keyed by content SHA-256 plus engine version. Model cross-file phases as Salsa queries (the salsa crate, as in rust-analyzer) with revision-based invalidation and early cutoff. Use stable item ids like rust-analyzer's AstId or CodeQL TRAP keys. Done = editing one method body re-runs Phases 1-5 for that file only, shown with a benchmark.

title: The token types are Java-centric and doc comments are never classified
evidence: No adapter emits TokenType::CommentDoc. Java maps block_comment and comment to CommentBlock (src/ingestion/adapter/java.rs:46-48), and the generic adapter maps comment to CommentLine (src/ingestion/adapter/generic.rs:46). The default TokenFilter keeps doc comments but drops block comments (src/core/types/source.rs:31-40), so Javadoc, KDoc and JSDoc never reach the corpus. The 'language-specific' TokenType range holds only Java variants (src/core/types/token.rs:64-68), two of which are never produced. The Java keyword list (java.rs:60-66) lacks sealed, permits and non-sealed, so include_anonymous (:75-77) drops them. The generic adapter maps any alphabetic kind, such as string_fragment, to Keyword (generic.rs:53-54).
impact: UML notes drawn from documentation and doc-aware queries are impossible. New language-specific tokens would collide in the 0x80 range, which is not split by language.
recommendation: Classify doc comments per language in the frontend (/**, ///, //!, Python docstring nodes). Key token extensions by (language, kind). Generate token maps from each grammar's node-types.json and fail CI on unmapped leaf kinds.

title: Branch edge types are inconsistent across loop and switch builders
evidence: The do-while taken branch is typed LoopBack, so that branch has a False edge with no True partner. A switch's no-match edge is typed False. for(;;) types its unconditional header-to-body edge True. CFGEdgeType has no way to mark an edge as both True and a back edge.
impact: CDG, PSA and diagram consumers that key on True/False see malformed conditional branches.
recommendation: Separate branch polarity from a back-edge flag. Use True/False for do-while, a Switch/Default kind for the no-match edge, and Uncond for for(;;).

title: assert statements and ternary expressions are treated as straight-line code
evidence: NN_JAVA_ASSERT_STMT and NN_TERNARY_EXPR fall through to add_stmt_to_current, so the assert's conditional AssertionError throw and the ternary's two arms never become branches. FLOW-08 covers && / || and switch expressions but not these two.
impact: Branch points and exceptional exits are missing from the CFG and CDG.
recommendation: Lower assert to `if (!cond) throw` (optionally behind an -ea flag), and lower ternaries to diamond sub-CFGs once an expression IR exists (FLOW-16).

title: Misleading algorithm names, invariant logs and missing Phase 6 timer
evidence: Anderson is a misspelling of Andersen. resolve_1cfa filters by receiver allocation and is not call-string 1-CFA. Phase 6 logs Invariants 1-4 as asserted after three checks, and logs a count mismatch as Invariant 1 verified. Invariant 2 cannot fail, because find_method_name_token never returns u32::MAX. Phase 6 skips PhaseTimer, so its duration is never reported.
impact: Names and logs overstate what is implemented and verified.
recommendation: Rename (AndersenPointsTo, resolve_by_receiver_alloc), report the mismatch as a warning, implement or drop the missing invariant, and use PhaseTimer.

title: Core type docs overstate layouts and leave sentinels undocumented
evidence: SSARecord is described as Cache-Aligned but has no repr or align attribute, and the fixed-size CallSite, CallEdge and SCCRecord have no repr(C). CFGEdgeType::from maps unknown bytes to Uncond without error. BasicBlock's u32::MAX/0 token sentinel for empty blocks is undocumented, and TRA maps it to token 0.
impact: Readers rely on layout guarantees that do not exist, and corrupt edge bytes go unnoticed.
recommendation: Add repr(C) with size asserts or drop the claims, implement TryFrom for CFGEdgeType, and document every sentinel.

title: IFDSResults taint tuple means different things to its producer and its consumer
evidence: ifds.rs stores (ssa_id, 1), where the u16 is a taint-source id. PSA feasibility reads the same u16 as a block id and treats every branch in block 1 as complex whenever any taint fact exists. IFDSResults documents neither field. FLOW-10 covers the stub logic itself, not this contract.
impact: PSA misclassifies block-1 branches and ignores tainted branches in all other blocks.
recommendation: Document the tuple and store the def block (or use a struct with named fields), and have PSA look up blocks through SSARecord.

title: Dead code and unused results across Phases 4-6
evidence: The ENTRY-to-EXIT fallback condition is always false, because the entry-to-first_real edge always exists. pred_lists, the _succs parameter, PendingPhi.target_ssa, block_phi_map, live_out, the returned ipdom, site_to_targets, MOD_ABSTRACT and the CallEdge type are never used. `receiver.is_none()` is unreachable, because a method_invocation always has a name child.
impact: Readers are misled about what is actually computed, and the work is wasted.
recommendation: Delete each item or wire it up (for example, persist ipdom and use block_phi_map).

title: STA deserialization allocates memory from untrusted counts and lengths
evidence: Header counts go straight into Vec::with_capacity, and each string length goes into read_exact_bytes, which allocates vec![0; len] before reading. CRC-64 is not a MAC, so a 72-byte file with symbol_count 0xFFFFFFFF and a recomputed checksum requests about 256 GiB. The CLI artifact inspector reaches this code.
impact: A crafted or corrupt .sta aborts the process instead of returning an error.
recommendation: Before allocating, check that count × record size fits in the remaining bytes, cap string lengths by the remaining bytes, and use try_reserve. Fuzz SymbolTableArtifact::deserialize.

title: Deserialization does no semantic validation, and the From<u8> enum conversions silently coerce unknown values
evidence: format_version is read but never compared with STA_FORMAT_VERSION. symbol_id is not checked to equal its index, and parent, child, sibling, type and scope ids are not range-checked. THRelation::from maps any unknown byte to TH_EXTENDS; unknown kinds similarly become SK_EXTERNAL, visibilities Package and scope kinds File. The optional package sections swallow read errors, and trailing bytes are ignored.
impact: A version mismatch or corruption produces plausible but wrong hierarchies instead of a load error.
recommendation: Reject unknown format versions. Implement TryFrom<u8> for these enums and fail on unknown values. Validate id ranges and the exact payload length, and add negative tests.

title: Per-class diagnostic logging at INFO level on the hot path
evidence: Pass 1 logs every discovered class at INFO ("[DIAG-PASS1] Class Discovered") and the first 100 nodes at DEBUG. log_event writes and flushes both log files whatever the console level, and the format! call runs first regardless. A 10k-class project produces 10k console lines and 20k flushed file writes, and class names pile up in the persistent log.
impact: Large inputs pay for avoidable I/O, the console is noisy, and source identifiers are kept across runs.
recommendation: Remove the DIAG logs, or demote them to TRACE behind a level check (a macro that skips formatting when disabled), and log one summary line per pass.

title: ScopeRecord.import_count is a u16 incremented without overflow checks
evidence: add_import_edge and add_import_mapping increment import_count, a u16, with plain `+= 1`. Pass 2 registers every file's imports on the shared root scope, so a project with more than 65,535 import lines overflows: debug builds panic and release builds wrap. Duplicate mappings are counted twice. The bug stays dormant until SYM-01 lets imports reach Pass 2.
impact: Once imports flow, large monorepos can crash Phase 3 in debug builds or serialize wrong counts.
recommendation: Use u32 or saturating_add, count distinct entries only, and register imports on each file's own scope.

title: Instance initializer blocks are never recognized
evidence: The adapter handles NN_JAVA_INSTANCE_INIT, but the Java reducer maps every block, including an initializer block in a class body, to NN_BLOCK. SK_INSTANCE_INIT is therefore never produced, and locals declared inside `{ ... }` initializers get the class as parent and live in the class scope.
impact: Initializer code is attributed to the class itself, and its locals look like class-scope declarations.
recommendation: Emit NN_JAVA_INSTANCE_INIT when a block's parent is class_body, and give it a method-like scope.

title: Several SymbolRecord fields are never filled in
evidence: type_param_count, flags and uml_meta_offset are always 0. def_node always equals decl_node, even for abstract and interface methods that have no body. Records carry no file id, so consumers decode it from first_token_id, which swept, package and external symbols do not have. AssociationDetector reads bit 0x08 of flags as an array flag that nothing ever sets.
impact: Record bytes are wasted, and array fields, generic arity and a symbol's file are unavailable.
recommendation: Set type_param_count and array/varargs flags from the AST, set def_node only when a body exists, store a file_id in the _reserved field, and define named constants for the flag bits.

title: Layout comments misdescribe the records, the magic number and the hierarchy encoding
evidence: SymbolRecord is called "cache-aligned" but is plain repr(C) with 4-byte alignment. UMLAssociationRecord is called 28 bytes but is 32 in memory; only the serialized form is 28. The type hierarchy is described as CSR but is written as a flat 9-byte edge list. The STA_MAGIC comment says "STA\x00\x01", but little-endian write_u64 puts 00 00 00 01 00 41 54 53 on disk. The u16::MAX "many" multiplicity is undocumented.
impact: External readers of the .sta format and maintainers get wrong expectations.
recommendation: Add align(64) or drop the alignment claim, and add const size assertions. Fix the CSR comments or implement CSR. Write the magic as a byte string, and add a MULT_UNBOUNDED constant.

title: NodeAttr has room for only 8 modifiers, so default, strictfp, non-sealed, varargs and Kotlin modifiers never reach symbols
evidence: NodeAttr packs modifiers into 8 bits (static through sealed). extract_modifiers builds SymbolModifiers from those bits alone, so STRICTFP, DEFAULT, NON_SEALED, VARARGS, DEPRECATED and RECORD_COMPONENT are unreachable. VISIBILITY_NONE and VISIBILITY_PACKAGE_PRIVATE both mean package access, and there is no Kotlin internal, open or override. This differs from CORE-03, which covers substring matching and the stub decoder.
impact: Interface default methods, varargs and Kotlin modifiers cannot be told apart in UML or symbol output.
recommendation: Widen the attribute word (u64, or a separate u16 modifier array), add the missing Java and Kotlin modifiers, and use a single package-private encoding.

title: close_node updates every open ancestor's token range, and that result is always overwritten
evidence: close_node walks the whole open_stack to merge the child's range (min/max) into every ancestor. The reducer already merges each child's returned (ft, lt) into its own range, and every ancestor's own close_node then overwrites its entry (line 164). The propagation is redundant O(depth) work per node.
impact: Deeply nested expressions make Phase 2 quadratic in nesting depth for no effect.
recommendation: Remove the ancestor loop, or propagate only to the parent, and assert in close_node that preorder_idx is the top of open_stack.

title: Phase 1 wraps columns above 65,535 while Phase 2 saturates them, so their sort keys disagree
evidence: walker.rs:59 uses `start.column as u16`, which wraps modulo 65,536. reducer.rs:56 uses `start.column.min(u16::MAX as usize) as u16`, which saturates at 65,535. On a minified line past column 65,535, Phase 2 builds keys that never match Phase 1's and falls back to an arbitrary token on the same line. This differs from CORE-05, which covers the cap itself.
impact: Nodes on very long lines are bound to the wrong tokens, corrupting ranges, names and traceability spans.
recommendation: Use one shared column-packing helper in both phases, ideally with a wider column field, and reject or flag files that exceed the limit.

title: Columns are tree-sitter byte offsets with mixed bases, which is undocumented
evidence: The walker stores `line: row + 1` (1-based) and `col: start.column` (a 0-based byte offset). With tabs or non-ASCII UTF-8 text, the byte column differs from the character or UTF-16 column that editors and LSP use. Neither token.rs nor the spec states the unit.
impact: L:C spans in traces and the web studio point to the wrong column on lines containing non-ASCII text.
recommendation: Document the unit. Either store character or UTF-16 columns, or convert in the traceability layer, and use consistent bases for line and column.

title: Phase 2 uses positions in the sorted forward index as token ids
evidence: Phase 2 reads Section 4, the forward table ordered by sort_key, and tok_table_lookup returns the binary-search index as the token id. Phase 1 token ids follow allocation order (SourceFileRecord.first_token_id and Section 5). The two coincide only while push order is already sorted, a dependency the spec itself admits.
impact: Any change to Phase 1 ordering, such as parallel ingestion or column wrap, silently desynchronizes AST token ranges from file token ranges.
recommendation: Resolve through the backward index and return the entry's token_id, or assert in finalize() that forward and backward order match, then drop the duplicate array.

title: Zero-width MISSING nodes become phantom tokens with empty text
evidence: walk_recursive emits every leaf without checking node.is_missing(). Tree-sitter error recovery inserts zero-width MISSING leaves (for example a missing `;` or identifier). These pass include_anonymous and map_node_type, are pushed with len 0 and are interned as an empty string. This differs from CORE-09: it is a concrete corruption of the corpus, not the general lack of an error model.
impact: Incomplete code produces fake punctuation and identifier tokens that downstream heuristics treat as real.
recommendation: Skip is_missing() leaves, or mark them in the sort-key flags byte, and count them as diagnostics.

title: Language detection ignores the adapter registry: ext_map is never read and detect() is a hardcoded static
evidence: register() fills ext_map, including a '*' key, but nothing reads it. detect() is an associated function with its own extension match, so a newly registered adapter's extensions are never detected. Overrides are looked up by the raw OsStr: case-sensitive, and a key with a leading dot never matches. IngestionStage builds its own registry, so callers cannot inject adapters.
impact: Adding a language means editing three places, and overrides silently fail for upper-case or dotted extensions.
recommendation: Make detect a method that uses ext_map, normalize override keys (lowercase, strip a leading dot), and let the manifest or the stage accept an AdapterRegistry.

title: The .tca string-header section is written but never used
evidence: write() emits a hash-sorted (fnv1a, offset) table at 12 B per string. read() parses it into str_headers and drops it, then rebuilds the interner by re-hashing and re-interning every stored string. String ids come back only because re-interning in storage order happens to reproduce them.
impact: The section wastes space and load time, and a duplicate string in storage would shift every later text_id.
recommendation: Either use the headers for zero-copy lookup (mmap plus binary search) or remove the section, and rebuild ids by position rather than by dedup.

title: TCA read() discards the filter flags, source-tree hash and timestamp; the tree hash ignores paths
evidence: read() binds _flags, _hash and _mtime (which is really the creation timestamp) and drops them, and the artifact has no fields to hold them. source_tree_hash hashes the per-file digests in path order without the paths themselves, so a rename that keeps the order goes unnoticed. The spec says SHA-256(sorted(...)) and promises LZ4 compression; neither is implemented.
impact: A reloaded corpus cannot be checked against its sources or its token filter, which blocks staleness checks.
recommendation: Store the filter, tree hash and timestamp in the artifact, include normalized paths in the tree hash, and align the spec with the code.

title: The TCA magic is written as a little-endian u64, so the file starts with reversed bytes
evidence: TCA_MAGIC = 0x544F4B434F525001 is documented as 'TOKCORP\x01', but write_u64 emits the bytes 01 50 52 4F 43 4B 4F 54, which read '\x01PROCKOT' (verified with Python struct). The .bpa writes its magic as a byte string, so the two formats use opposite conventions.
impact: File-type sniffing, hex inspection and external tools see a reversed signature.
recommendation: Write magics as byte strings everywhere (b'TOKCORP\x01'), and keep a compatibility reader for existing v1 files.

title: The .bpa header has a hardcoded file_count, an ignored version and no per-file root table
evidence: write() always stores file_count = 1 and format_version = 1, and read() discards both. node_types is written without a length prefix, unlike the other arrays. Nothing records which NN_MODULE root belongs to which file; consumers infer it from token ranges, which fails for nodes that have no tokens.
impact: Future format changes cannot be detected, the header is wrong, and mapping nodes to files is fragile.
recommendation: Write the real file count plus a per-file (file_id, root_preorder) table, validate the version on read, and length-prefix every array.

title: Phase 2 hand-parses .tca bytes with hardcoded offsets and cannot take the in-memory corpus
evidence: ASTStage::run accepts only a MemoryMappedFile. It re-implements the TCA layout (header offsets 12..16 and 16..18, record offset 36, alignment math) instead of calling TokenCorpusSerializer or using the TokenCorpusArtifact that Phase 1 just returned. It also builds an unused Phase1Registry. This differs from CORE-07, which covers missing validation.
impact: Two independent TCA parsers must change in lockstep, and every run forces a disk round-trip.
recommendation: Have ASTStage take a &TokenCorpusArtifact, or a zero-copy TCA view shared with the serializer, and delete the unused registry.

title: Phase 2 reserves memory for 2x token_count nodes, taken from the unvalidated header
evidence: tok_table reserves 16 B per header token, then BPASTBuilder::new(token_count * 2) reserves four preorder arrays (17 B per node) plus BP words, about 34 B per token, although kept nodes are usually fewer than tokens. token_count comes straight from the header with no check, so 0xFFFFFFFF requests over 140 GB and aborts. This differs from CORE-07 because it over-allocates even on valid input.
impact: Large corpora commit far more memory than needed, and a corrupt header aborts the process instead of returning Err.
recommendation: Estimate capacity from file sizes or grow dynamically, cap the reservation, and validate counts against the mapped length before reserving.

title: The interner hashes the full text but stores a truncated copy, and its u32 counters can wrap
evidence: intern() hashes all of the text, but store_string keeps only 65,535 bytes. For longer input `lookup_text(id) == text` never matches, so every call appends another copy. Storage offsets are `storage.len() as u32` and count is a u32, so both wrap past 4 GiB or 4 billion strings. Phase 1 truncates tokens before interning, but paths and other API callers are exposed.
impact: Repeated long strings grow memory without bound, and very large pools return wrong strings.
recommendation: Truncate or reject before hashing, use u64 offsets or checked arithmetic, and return an error when a limit is exceeded.

title: The sort key's 'reserved' flags byte silently carries a duplicate counter that wraps at 256
evidence: The doc says bits 7..0 are reserved and zero, but Phase 1 ORs a dup_count into them when consecutive tokens share (file, line, col), for example zero-width tokens. dup_count is a u8 incremented with wrapping_add, so the 256th duplicate collides with the first. unpack_sort_key drops the byte. This differs from CORE-05.
impact: A collision aborts Phase 1 through Invariant 2, and readers cannot tell duplicate tokens apart.
recommendation: Document the byte as a discriminator, error out on overflow instead of wrapping, return it from unpack_sort_key, and remove the cause (no zero-width or wrapped tokens).

title: Log files grow without bound, session IDs collide within a second, and setup errors are swallowed
evidence: The persistent log is opened in append mode and never rotated or size-capped. The session ID has one-second resolution, so concurrent runs share an ID while both truncate the same session file. create_dir_all and open failures are discarded through `let _` and `.ok()`, and an unknown OPENHEART_LOG value is ignored without notice. This differs from CORE-13.
impact: Long-lived deployments fill disks, concurrent runs interleave their logs, and misconfiguration goes unnoticed.
recommendation: Add size-based rotation, build session IDs from the PID plus a nanosecond timestamp (or randomness), and warn on stderr when a log file cannot be opened or OPENHEART_LOG is invalid.

title: Infallible From<u8> conversions turn corrupt bytes into plausible values
evidence: Unknown bytes map to defaults: THRelation to TH_EXTENDS, SymbolKind to SK_EXTERNAL, CFGEdgeType to Uncond, ScopeKind to File, SymbolVisibility to Package, AssocKind to None, ASTNodeType to NN_UNKNOWN, and LangId and TokenType to Unknown. TokenType also uses from_u8/as_u8 while the other enums implement From.
impact: A corrupt or newer-version artifact yields fake inheritance edges and wrong kinds instead of an error.
recommendation: Implement TryFrom<u8> returning an error for unknown values, use it in every deserializer, and keep the lossy conversion only where it is explicitly wanted.

title: Record layout comments are wrong, and three repr(C) records have no size test
evidence: UMLAssociationRecord is documented as '28-byte fixed', but its repr(C) layout is 32 B, with padding after assoc_kind and is_navigable plus tail padding (checked with Python ctypes). SymbolRecord claims to be cache-aligned but has alignment 4. SSARecord claims '16-Byte Cache-Aligned' without repr(C) or align. Only SourceFileRecord, TokenRecord and TokenEntry have size_of tests.
impact: Anyone mapping these records zero-copy from disk will misread fields, and the comments mislead layout work.
recommendation: Reorder the fields (or pack carefully), fix the comments, and add size_of and align_of tests for SymbolRecord, ScopeRecord and UMLAssociationRecord.

title: Several TokenType and ASTNodeType variants are never produced
evidence: grep finds no producer for TokenType::TypeParameter, LabeledStmt, JavaGenericDiamond or JavaSealedKeyword; LabeledStmt and TypeParameter are syntactic categories, not lexical ones. NN_PATTERN_MATCH and NN_SYNTHETIC are never emitted. NN_ELSE_CLAUSE, NN_YIELD_STMT and NN_JAVA_INSTANCE_INIT are covered by CORE2-03, CORE2-04 and CORE2-05.
impact: Consumers may write handling for kinds that never occur, and the alphabet misstates what Phases 1 and 2 emit.
recommendation: Remove or implement each variant, keep syntactic kinds out of the lexical alphabet, and document which adapter produces each value.

title: Flag constants in core types are never set, so is_polymorphic() always returns false
evidence: CALL_SITE_FLAG_IS_POLYMORPHIC, HAS_NULL_RECEIVER and IS_TAIL_CALL are never set (call_sites.rs:43 has `let flags = 0u8;`), so CallSite::is_polymorphic() is always false. SSA_FLAG_IS_PARAM_DEF, FIELD_DEF, RETURN_VAL and CONST, and CG_EDGE_REFLECTION, have no users outside core/types.
impact: The API advertises polymorphism, parameter and constant facts that are never computed.
recommendation: Set the flags where the information exists (virtual sites with several targets, parameter definitions), or delete the constants and the predicate.

title: The Artifact trait is implemented only by the token corpus and fixes the file count at u16
evidence: The doc says the trait is implemented by pipeline stage output artifacts, but only TokenCorpusArtifact implements it. token_count() and file_count() -> u16 are TCA concepts that do not fit the other artifacts, and the u16 writes the CORE-05 cap into the API.
impact: The trait adds no generic capability such as version checks, hashing or I/O, and it misleads readers.
recommendation: Redefine the trait around shared needs (magic, format_version, content_hash, write/read) and implement it for every artifact, or remove it.

title: The core module depends on every phase, inverting the layering
evidence: core::pipeline imports ast, cfg, cg, ingestion, psa, scpg, ssa, symbol, tra and uma, while all of those import core::types, core::io and core::logger. So 'core' is not a foundation layer, and a change to any phase touches the core API.
impact: Phases cannot be split into crates or tested in isolation, and dependency cycles stay hidden.
recommendation: Move SCPGPipelineBuilder and PipelineArtifacts to a top-level pipeline or driver module, and limit core to types, io and logging.

title: Error messages Debug-format strings and paths, which double-escapes them
evidence: execute() wraps String errors with `{:?}` (for example 'Phase 1 Ingestion Error: {:?}') and formats io::Error the same way; ingestion formats paths with `{:?}`. A Windows path therefore surfaces in quotes with backslashes doubled and then doubled again, and io errors appear as `Os { code: 2, kind: NotFound, ... }`.
impact: Users see escaped, hard-to-read messages, unlike the CLI path, which uses `{}`.
recommendation: Format with `{}` and path.display(), or adopt a typed error enum with Display messages (thiserror is already a dependency).

title: The library pipeline writes graph.scpg where the CLI writes unified.scpg, and exposes no filter or override settings
evidence: SCPGPipelineBuilder names its Phase 10 output graph.scpg, while cmd_analyze and the usage text use unified.scpg. execute() always calls SourceManifest::new, so TokenFilter and language_overrides cannot be set through the builder. This is a concrete divergence on top of CORE-14's copy-paste finding.
impact: Tools that look for unified.scpg miss library output, and comment or doc-comment policy cannot be configured.
recommendation: Define the artifact file names once as shared constants, and add with_filter and with_language_override to the builder (or let it accept a SourceManifest).

title: BinaryReader allocates before reading, and the alignment helpers divide by zero
evidence: read_exact_bytes allocates `vec![0u8; len]` before read_exact, so a corrupt length allocates first and fails afterwards, and there is no remaining() to validate counts. align_to(0) and skip_alignment(0) compute `% 0` and panic. The .bpa serializer and Phase 2 bypass these helpers with hand-rolled try_into().unwrap() slicing. This differs from CORE-07: it is about hardening the helpers.
impact: Every reader built on these helpers inherits allocate-then-fail behavior, and the formats use inconsistent parsing code.
recommendation: Add remaining() and ensure(len) checks, read through take(len) into a growing Vec, reject an alignment of 0, and port the .bpa code to BinaryReader and BinaryWriter.

title: Loading a .bpa rebuilds rank/select and the sparse table, and both writers buffer the whole artifact
evidence: read() loads the persisted jump table, which could be rebuilt in one O(n) pass, yet rebuilds RankSelectIndex and the O(n log n) SparseTableRMQ on every load. Both writers assemble the entire file in a Vec, compute the CRC over it and only then write, holding a full second copy in memory. This differs from CORE-04 (resident size) and CORE-10 (source reads).
impact: Every load of a large AST costs O(n log n) time, and serialization roughly doubles peak memory.
recommendation: Persist the expensive indexes or build them lazily, and stream writes through a writer that updates the CRC as it goes.

title: BPASTArtifact::depth is 1-based while the builder's depth is 0-based, and four accessors are unused
evidence: depth() computes 2*rank1(open)-open-1, which gives 1 for a root, while BPASTBuilder::current_depth(), which is passed to classify, gives 0 for a root. Neither documents its base. grep finds no callers and no tests for depth, subtree_size, is_leaf or BPASTArtifact::lca.
impact: Off-by-one errors are likely once these APIs are used, and their correctness is unverified.
recommendation: Document a single depth base (0 for roots) and use it in both places, and add unit tests for each accessor against a naive pointer tree.

title: BPASTBuilder exposes mutable internals and panics instead of returning errors
evidence: All builder fields (bp, preorder, open_stack, node_count) are pub. close_node pops whatever is on top of the stack without checking that it matches preorder_idx. finalize() and JumpTableBuilder::build use assert! and expect on unbalanced input, so a buggy adapter crashes the process.
impact: Adapter bugs produce panics or silently malformed BP sequences rather than errors that can be diagnosed.
recommendation: Make the fields private, verify last-in-first-out closing in close_node, and return Result from finalize and from the jump-table builder.

title: Phase 1 records file size from metadata read before the content, and some errors omit the file path
evidence: file_size_bytes comes from fs::metadata, taken before fs::read, so it can differ from the content that was hashed. The second read fails with 'Read error: {}' and a parse failure reports 'Tree-sitter parse returned None'; neither message names the file.
impact: Recorded sizes can contradict the hashes, and failures in large trees are hard to locate.
recommendation: Use content.len() for the size, and include path.display() in every per-file error with map_err at the call site.

title: Low-level accessors return silent sentinel values for invalid input
evidence: get_bit returns 0 (a close paren) past the end. range_min returns position 0 for out-of-range bounds. lookup_text returns an empty slice for invalid ids or corrupt offsets. node_type, node_attr, token_range and parent return NN_UNKNOWN, 0, (MAX, 0) and MAX. None of them logs or distinguishes bad input from legitimate values.
impact: Index bugs and corrupt artifacts show up as wrong results far from their cause.
recommendation: Return Option or Result from these accessors, or debug_assert on out-of-range input, and keep sentinel fallbacks only at API boundaries.

title: security-architecture.md calls CRC-64 tamper protection and misstates the interner bounds
evidence: Lines 16-20 present CRC-64 as 'Tamper Protection', but an attacker can simply recompute a CRC, and the SHA-256 digests written in ingestion/mod.rs:56-97 are never re-verified. Line 27 says u16 lengths prevent unbounded allocation. In fact interner.rs:99 truncates tokens over 64 KiB and line 67 then never matches them, so each occurrence is stored again. ENG-17 covered only lines 11-12, 26 and 34.
impact: Readers assume tamper evidence that does not exist, and long tokens bloat storage.
recommendation: Call it corruption detection or add a keyed MAC. Verify the SHA-256 digests on load. Store full token text or reject oversize tokens explicitly.

title: README and codebase-guide list artifact magic headers that do not exist
evidence: README.md:113-124 and codebase-guide.md:272-283 list TCA\0, BPA\0, SSA\0 and so on. The code uses 'TOKCORP\x01', b'BPAST\0\x01\0', 'SSA1', b'OPENHPSA' and b'OPENHUMA'. u64 magics are written little-endian (binary.rs:40-41), so the STA, CFA, CGA and TCA bytes appear reversed on disk. CFA_MAGIC contains '0' where its comment says \0, and phase2 spec:946 shows a 15-digit hex magic.
impact: Anyone who writes a reader or file-type detector from these docs gets it wrong.
recommendation: Define magics as byte arrays written verbatim, generate the table from the constants, and fix the source comments.

title: Docs give contradictory token and traceability record layouts
evidence: CHANGELOG.md:53 describes the sort_key as 48/24/8 bits, which is 80 bits in a u64; the code packs 16/24/16 plus a reserved byte (token.rs:121-124). traceability:29 calls the key u48, and line 36 gives a '10-byte' backward-index entry whose fields sum to 9 bytes (the real entry is 16). succinct_structures.md:121-122 says 12 and 10 bytes, where both are 16. The UMLLink struct in traceability:57-68 does not match tra/types.rs:99-109.
impact: Contributors who write readers or review invariants work from wrong layouts.
recommendation: Keep one layout reference generated from the const asserts and link every doc to it.

title: The 'cache-line aligned' TokenRecord and 'hardware-friendly' CRC claims are inaccurate
evidence: ADR-003 (technical-decisions.md:25-29), CHANGELOG.md:50 and overview.md:9 call the 16-byte TokenRecord cache-line aligned. It is repr(C) with 8-byte alignment (token.rs:136-145), and the .tca token table is only 8-byte aligned, so a record can straddle two cache lines. ADR-004 (33-37) calls the CRC 'fast hardware-friendly', but crc64_ecma is a bit-at-a-time loop (serializer.rs:16-29).
impact: The ADRs' performance rationale does not describe the actual implementation.
recommendation: Use #[repr(C, align(16))] with 64-byte section alignment, or reword the claim. Switch to a table-driven (slicing-by-8) CRC.

title: architecture.md lists ROBDD and BP operations that do not exist
evidence: architecture.md:119 says the ROBDD layer uses complement edges, but ROBDDNode (node.rs:44-58) has no complement bit; flag bits 2-15 are reserved. architecture.md:106 and succinct_structures.md:32-34 promise O(1) findopen, findclose and enclose over the BP bitstring. No such primitives exist, and first_child and next_sibling live on the builder's arrays (builder.rs:58-71).
impact: Readers credit the engine with algorithms it does not have.
recommendation: Remove these claims, or implement the operations with tests.

title: language_count header field is hardcoded to 1
evidence: src/scpg/serializer/mod.rs:149 writes 1u32 as language_count whatever the input. tca.file_records carry a language_id per file, and LangId defines Java, Kotlin and eight more (src/core/types/token.rs:6-18). docs/plans/phase10.md:27 specifies 'number of distinct source languages ingested'.
impact: Mixed Java and Kotlin projects are recorded as single-language, so the header metadata cannot be trusted.
recommendation: Count the distinct non-Unknown language_id values in tca.file_records and write that number. Add a test with one .java and one .kt file that expects 2.

title: EngineBuilder cannot build anything and duplicates SCPGPipelineBuilder
evidence: src/scpg/api/builder.rs:5-35 holds output_dir, cache_capacity and enable_mmap with two setters. It has no build() or open(), no setter for enable_mmap, and no code reads any field. It is public API (src/scpg/mod.rs:16). SCPGPipelineBuilder (src/core/pipeline.rs:97-114) does the real work and defaults to temp_dir instead of ./scpg_out. This is broader than SCPG-14's cache-capacity point.
impact: A public configuration path does nothing, and the two builders have conflicting defaults.
recommendation: Implement EngineBuilder::build() and open(path) honoring cache_capacity and enable_mmap (adding with_mmap), or remove it and keep a single builder with a documented default output directory.

title: Slice traversals scan the whole site_to_edge_map for every visited symbol
evidence: backward_slice scans every cga.site_to_edge_map entry for each popped symbol to find callers (src/scpg/query/slice.rs:28-32), and forward_slice does the same for callees (:64-68). That is O(V·E). The CGA already has caller_csr/callee_csr indexed by symbol id, with edges_of() (src/core/types/cg.rs:127-137; src/cg/mod.rs:110). SCPG-09 and SCPG-15 cover only CFL and impact.
impact: Slices on large call graphs become quadratic and hold the engine's global mutex the whole time.
recommendation: Use cga.caller_csr.edges_of(sym) and cga.callee_csr.edges_of(sym) for O(degree) neighbor lookup, or build a reverse adjacency once per CGA. Note that the CSR omits out-of-range external callees.

title: StringTable section omits the interner's offset index
evidence: src/scpg/serializer/mod.rs:62 writes only tca.interner.get_storage_bytes(), that is, u16-length-prefixed strings (src/ingestion/interner.rs:95-102). The offsets array (interner.rs:23, get_offsets at :123) and the string count are not written, so resolving a text_id needs an O(n) scan from the start.
impact: The only section with real content cannot support the O(1) name lookups that diagrams and navigation need.
recommendation: Write the count and a u32 offsets array before the storage blob (or as their own section) and document the layout. Test: round-trip the interner and compare lookup_text for every id.

title: Field and method modifiers are truncated from u16 to u8
evidence: `modifiers: child.modifiers as u8` drops bits 8 to 15: DEFAULT, SEALED, NON_SEALED, VARARGS, BRIDGE, SYNTHETIC, DEPRECATED and RECORD_COMPONENT. Today only SEALED is ever set (pass1_discovery.rs:940), so nothing is lost yet, but ClassRecord keeps the full u16 while member records cannot.
impact: Default methods, varargs and deprecation can never be shown once Phase 3 starts setting them, and the loss is silent.
recommendation: Widen FieldRecord and MethodRecord modifiers to u16 and bump the format version, or debug_assert that the high byte is zero.

title: message_kind stores raw call-graph edge codes, and the entry message reuses call_site_id 0
evidence: message_kind = site.call_type, which holds DIRECT 0, VIRTUAL 2, CONSTRUCTOR 4 and so on, not UML message sorts. The actor message hard-codes kind 0 and call_site_id 0, and 0 is also the first real call site's id. There are no MESSAGE_KIND_* or fragment-kind constants, and no exporter reads message_kind.
impact: Create and async messages cannot be told apart, and call_site_id 0 is ambiguous.
recommendation: Define MESSAGE_KIND sync/async/create/reply and FRAGMENT_KIND constants, map CG_EDGE_CONSTRUCTOR to create, and use u32::MAX for the synthetic entry call site.

title: The class extractor treats path_str_offset as an interner id, which a disk-loaded TCA does not hold
evidence: The test-file and filename-stem checks look up tca.interner.lookup_text(file_records[fid].path_str_offset). The TCA writer replaces that field with a byte offset into the path section, and the reader skips the path bytes without interning them. Phase 9 currently always receives the in-memory TCA, so the problem is latent.
impact: Running Phase 9 on a reloaded .tca would apply the test and stem filters to unrelated strings.
recommendation: Give TokenCorpusArtifact a file_path(fid) accessor that works in both modes, and use it in class_diagram. Add a test that runs Phase 9 on a reloaded .tca.

title: Every CLI command creates log files in the current directory
evidence: main.rs:488 calls init_logger_from_env, which opens ./openheart_persistent.log (append) and ./openheart_session.log (logger.rs:110-112), even for help, inspect and server. analyze then re-initializes into OUTPUT_DIR (main.rs:129), leaving stray files in the CWD. The server appends all pipeline logs to the CWD files for its whole lifetime, with no rotation.
impact: Repos fill up with log files, read-only CWDs fail silently, and server log files grow without limit.
recommendation: Enable file logging only for analyze and server, with an explicit --log-dir and size-based rotation. Keep help and inspect console-only.

title: Command output goes through the logger and can be silenced
evidence: inspect results and the analyze summary are printed with log_info (main.rs:311-342, 354-475). OPENHEART_LOG=warn or off (logger.rs:98-107) suppresses them, so openheart inspect prints nothing and exits 0.
impact: Users and scripts lose the command's main output when they lower log verbosity.
recommendation: Print results to stdout directly (optionally as --json) and keep the logger for diagnostics.

title: Artifact bytes depend on how the source path was spelled
evidence: cmd_analyze passes paths exactly as given or joined (main.rs:104-111, 151), and ingestion interns them into the .tca (ingestion/mod.rs:137-138). 'analyze ./src', 'analyze src' and an absolute path therefore produce different .tca bytes, CRC hash links and SCPG hashes. Absolute paths also embed the user's home directory.
impact: Hashes are not reproducible across machines or invocations, and local paths leak into shared artifacts.
recommendation: Store paths relative to the source root with forward slashes and record the root separately. Test that ./src and src give the same SCPG hash.

title: No file-count or file-size caps although file ids are 16-bit
evidence: The server passes every collected file to ingestion (server.rs:484-515) with no count or size limit. Ingestion casts file_id to u16 (ingestion/mod.rs:70, 123), and Phase 2 reads file_count as u16 (ast/mod.rs:59). Repositories with more than 65,535 matching files therefore wrap ids silently. Differs from SRV-04: the results are corrupted, not just slow.
impact: Large monorepos give corrupted cross-file results instead of a clear error.
recommendation: Reject or shard inputs above 65,535 files or above a per-file size limit with an explicit error, and make the limits configurable.

title: Security doc's input-bounds claims contradict the code
evidence: docs/security-architecture.md:26 says lines and columns are capped. In fact build_sort_key masks the line with 0x00FFFFFF after only a debug_assert (token.rs:122-123), and the walker truncates columns with 'as u16' (walker.rs:59). Line 27 says u16 length headers prevent unbounded allocation, but the interner silently truncates text beyond 65,535 bytes (interner.rs:99-101).
impact: Wrong positions on huge or minified files are neither documented nor expected.
recommendation: Implement saturation or explicit errors, and document the truncation behavior accurately.

title: Hand-rolled server JSON breaks on error text and control characters, and session temp directories leak
evidence: Error responses splice messages into JSON without escaping (server.rs:529-533, 543, 550-553, 601). Ingestion errors embed `{:?}`-formatted paths that contain quotes and backslashes (ingestion/mod.rs:52,54), and lines 496-502 insert target_dir.display(), derived from the attacker-chosen repo name, unescaped. escape_json_str (701-707) handles only backslash, double quote, newline, carriage return and tab, so any other control character in a file name corrupts success responses too. The early returns at 527-605 skip remove_dir_all (693), leaking one openheart_sess_* directory per failed request.
impact: Clients get JSON parse errors instead of diagnostics, and repeated failing requests gradually fill the temp volume.
recommendation: Build every response with serde_json::json! (already a dependency) and a typed error body. Hold the session directory in a tempfile::TempDir (move tempfile out of dev-dependencies) so that every exit path cleans up, and cap total temp usage per job.

title: The modifier and visibility model cannot carry half of SymbolModifiers or Kotlin visibility
evidence: NodeAttr has room for only 8 modifier bits, so DEFAULT, STRICTFP, NON_SEALED, VARARGS, DEPRECATED, SYNTHETIC and RECORD_COMPONENT can never be set. There is no Kotlin internal visibility and no bits for open, override, data, suspend or lateinit. default_visibility(kind) is not told the enclosing kind, so interface members cannot default to public. This differs from SYM-15, where extraction never runs at all.
impact: Even once extraction is fixed, default methods, varargs, sealed hierarchies and Kotlin visibility are lost.
recommendation: Carry modifiers in a wider attribute or a side table, add an Internal visibility and Kotlin modifier bits, and pass the enclosing kind to default_visibility.

title: Dependency edges come only from field types, and TH_CREATES is never emitted
evidence: THRelation::TH_CREATES is defined, but no pass produces it, and TH_USES edges come only from field types. Parameter types, return types, local and thrown-exception types, and `new T()` expressions produce no dependency edges.
impact: UML dependency arrows and coupling metrics miss most dependencies between classes.
recommendation: Emit TH_USES from method signatures and locals and TH_CREATES from NN_NEW_EXPR targets. De-duplicate per (from, to, relation) and keep these edges separate from inheritance edges.

title: Phase 3 runs single-threaded and re-hashes inputs that Phase 2 already hashed
evidence: All passes run sequentially, and Pass 1 makes one pass over the nodes plus two full token sweeps, although discovery, package parsing and name extraction are independent per file. build() recomputes CRC-64 over the whole TCA and BPA, even though Phase 2 already stored the TCA hash in bpa.tca_hash.
impact: Phase 3 time grows linearly with corpus size, with no parallel speed-up on large projects.
recommendation: Split per-file work across threads (rayon) and merge ids deterministically. Reuse bpa.tca_hash and compare it (see SYM2-26). Fold the package scan into the primary walk.

title: Interner and string-pool layouts waste memory
evidence: Each probe slot is (u64, u32), padded to 16 B, so the initial 65,536-slot table takes 1 MiB before any string is added. Storage keeps a u16 length prefix per string and also a separate u32 offsets array, so each length is effectively stored twice. The .tca then adds a 12 B header per string.
impact: Phase 1 holds about twice the necessary index memory for string-heavy corpora.
recommendation: Use (u32 hash fragment, u32 id) slots, derive lengths from consecutive offsets, and size the table from the expected number of unique strings.

title: Token classification runs the same string match twice per leaf
evidence: For anonymous leaves, include_anonymous calls map_node_type and the walker then calls it again, so two long match chains run per token. rustc lowers such matches to length and memcmp comparisons, not the 'perfect hash' the spec claims. walk_cst sizes its Vec from the root's child count, and its _source parameter is unused.
impact: Adds measurable per-token CPU in the hottest Phase 1 loop.
recommendation: Precompute a TokenType table indexed by node.kind_id() once per language, look it up once per leaf, and size the Vec from the source length.

title: tok_table_lookup binary-searches the whole corpus for every kept node
evidence: Every Keep node does a binary search over the tokens of all files, although nodes arrive in source order within a single file whose token range is known from first_token_id and file_token_count. This differs from CORE-12, which covers the lossy fallback.
impact: Phase 2 costs O(nodes x log tokens) instead of near-linear time.
recommendation: Restrict the search to the file's slice, and keep a forward-moving cursor with galloping search as the DFS advances.

title: Sources are assumed to be UTF-8, with no BOM or encoding handling
evidence: Files are read as raw bytes and passed to tree-sitter, and token text is interned as raw bytes. No code strips a UTF-8 BOM or decodes UTF-16 or Latin-1/Windows-1252 (grep finds none), and there is no javac-style encoding option. Downstream from_utf8 checks silently skip tokens that are not valid UTF-8.
impact: Legacy Windows-encoded Java files can yield ERROR nodes, shifted first-line columns and silently dropped identifiers.
recommendation: Detect and strip BOMs, support UTF-16 via its BOM, add a manifest encoding option that transcodes to UTF-8 before parsing, and record the encoding per file.

title: Query answers lack witness paths, distances and edge-kind filters
evidence: is_reachable returns only a bool (src/scpg/query/cfl.rs:10); impact_set and the slices return flat sorted Vec<u32> (src/scpg/query/impact.rs:31-33, src/scpg/query/slice.rs:42-44). The site_to_edge_map tuples carry no edge kind, although callee_csr.edge_types exists (src/core/types/cg.rs:120-124). So no query can exclude REFLECTION or DYNAMIC edges or report the call chain.
impact: Users cannot see why A reaches B, cannot verify results, and cannot tune precision.
recommendation: Return an optional witness path (from a BFS parent map), per-node distance for slices and impact, and accept a CG_EDGE_* mask on all graph queries.
